body:
MONAD Formal Mathematics
The Lean library defines MONAD’s mathematical objects and proves their properties. Use this guide to locate a definition, match paper notation to Lean, or maintain the library. The paper explains the same mathematics through one TeX companion per module.
lean-toolchain pins Lean 4; lakefile.toml pins mathlib to its matching v4.34.0 commit. lake-manifest.json records the transitive dependency revisions.
For a first encounter with the definitions, read a preservation claim in Lean. It carries a four-state example through ProbeFamily, Factors, Sufficient, the observational quotient and the compression obstruction. The product worked example supplies the mathematical interpretation without requiring Lean. The index below is for locating the exact branch after that orientation.
Organization and parity
Every mathematical module has the same relative path and stem in both trees:
formal/MonadFormal/Quotient.lean
paper/MonadFormal/Quotient.tex

Dependencies are imported, never reimplemented. General definitions live in Sandbox; specialized modules add hypotheses and reuse those definitions. The TeX companions carry leanproof and leandef bindings to fully qualified Lean declarations. The bindings do not add code identifiers to the typeset mathematics. Use stable result names and labels for references. The same rule applies below a module: Repair/Optimal.lean mirrors Repair/Optimal.tex, and Repair/Supplement.lean mirrors Repair/Supplement.tex. Parent modules own shared interfaces; children import them rather than restating their definitions.
The correspondence checker verifies both directions of the module/companion map, rejects duplicate inclusions and stale or duplicate public imports, and checks every displayed proof's binding, declaration resolution, trusted axiom dependencies, and local notation rules. It cannot infer that prose and Lean have identical hypotheses: that statement-level review remains mandatory. A theorem about finite states cannot discharge a measurable-space claim merely because its name matches.
Contents
Module	TeX companion (same stem)	Result	
Sandbox	Sandbox.tex	Probe families, equivalence, factorization and sufficiency.	
Quotient	Quotient.tex	Exact quotient, universal property, unique descent and relabeling.	
Monotonicity	Monotonicity.tex	Family growth refines equivalence.	
NoGo	NoGo.tex	Joint separation plus sufficiency forces injectivity.	
Defect	Defect.tex	Empty extension defect is equivalent to pulled-back sufficiency.	
Extension	Extension.tex	Covered-family closure, non-recovery and fiber constancy.	
Refinement	Refinement.tex	Least pair refinement, obtainability and carrier extension.	
Counterexample	Counterexample.tex	Old-bit revelation on an unchanged carrier.	
Budget	Budget.tex	Residual budgets, one-step recurrence and concatenation.	
Abstraction	Abstraction.tex	Exact partition backward-completeness correspondence.	
Repair	Repair.tex	Adaptive feasibility, non-recovery and free-information bounds.	
Repair/Optimal	Repair/Optimal.tex	Attained minimum cost, productive-query Bellman equation and cardinality-founded recursion.	
Repair/Supplement	Repair/Supplement.tex	Exact side-information alphabet and binary-length bounds; question-timing obstruction.	
Approximation	Approximation.tex	Normalized measurable-test total variation and Markov contraction on general measurable spaces.	
Approximation/Events	Approximation/Events.tex	Event/test equivalence by layer-cake integration; zero distance is equality of measures.	
Approximation/Simulation	Approximation/Simulation.tex	Common-kernel deficiency, bounded-risk transfer with explicit tolerance, and composition without assumed minimizers.	
Profile	Profile.tex	Protocol-record correspondence and postprocessing.	
Influence	Influence.tex	Deterministic protocol monotonicity and nontransitivity.	
Entropy	Entropy.tex	Measure-theoretic entropy conservation with integrability.	
Witnesses	Witnesses.tex	Pairwise/joint obstruction, macro intervention and threshold counterexamples; Bernoulli measures realize the same general total variation.	
Temporal	Temporal.tex	Banach-space variation of constants, exact hidden-state memory and terminal-future integrals, and the paired-state derivative.	
Temporal/MixedBoundary	Temporal/MixedBoundary.tex	Actual mixed-delay path, exact existence criterion, exhaustive resonance obstruction, and separate terminal compatibility.	
Temporal/Variational	Temporal/Variational.tex	Coercive Hilbert-space minimization, stationarity and exact energy gap.	
Temporal/Variational/Interval	Temporal/Variational/Interval.tex	Bounded primitive and shifted-difference operators, endpoint-constrained absolutely continuous paths, integral energy identity, unique minimizing velocity and weak Euler equation.	
Temporal/Variational/Paths	Temporal/Variational/Paths.tex	Exact correspondence with the full admissible H¹ path class; energy invariance and uniqueness of the minimizing path on [0,1].	
Temporal/Variational/Shift	Temporal/Variational/Shift.tex	Shifted-difference adjoint with separate forward/backward boundary supports and an L² force.	
Temporal/Variational/Regularity	Temporal/Variational/Regularity.tex	Mean-zero orthogonality, absolutely continuous integration by parts, and velocity regularity derived from the weak equation.	
Temporal/Variational/Euler	Temporal/Variational/Euler.tex	Nonlocal Euler equation for the unique minimizing path, with an absolutely continuous velocity and an L² second derivative almost everywhere.	
Information	Information.tex	KL mutual information on probability laws, measurable and Markov processing, single-letter capacity and admissible input costs.	
Information/Likelihood	Information/Likelihood.tex	Joint-density pullback and exact extended-valued relative-entropy transport on arbitrary measurable carriers, without disintegration.	
Information/Input	Information/Input.tex	General deterministic coarse-graining identity, capacity comparison, cost transport and measurable-section realizability; separate standard-Borel conditional-law reconstruction.	
Information/Testing	Information/Testing.tex	Actual Bayes-risk optimization over all randomized tests, with an attained likelihood-ratio rule and finite-alphabet overlap formula.	
Information/Testing/Chernoff	Information/Testing/Chernoff.tex	Prior-weighted finite-sample bound, independent-product tensorization, coefficient bounds and extended-valued information with exact support cases.	
Information/Testing/Tilted	Information/Testing/Tilted.tex	Actual common-support tilted laws, continuous endpoint extension, attained minimum, directional optimality and likelihood transport.	
Information/Testing/Sampling	Information/Testing/Sampling.tex	Product-law mean and variance, Chebyshev concentration and an explicit typical-set sample budget.	
Information/Testing/Converse	Information/Testing/Converse.tex	Matching finite-sample lower bound with exponential slack, including endpoint minimizers.	
Information/Testing/Exponent	Information/Testing/Exponent.tex	Full extended-valued finite-alphabet Chernoff exponent for fixed positive priors; unequal and disjoint supports retained.	
Information/Testing/Conditional	Information/Testing/Conditional.tex	Exact optimal risk from a restriction likelihood identity, on arbitrary measurable spaces, and independent-product transport.	
Information/Testing/MovingSupport	Information/Testing/MovingSupport.tex	Actual Lebesgue-uniform interval laws, exact finite-sample risk and a nontrivial inverse-sample local-testing limit.	
Information/Testing/Hellinger	Information/Testing/Hellinger.tex	Actual probability laws from nonnegative unit L² roots, uniqueness, affinity identity and Hellinger separation.	
Information/Testing/Hellinger/Variation	Information/Testing/Hellinger/Variation.tex	Density formula for the existing operational TV and both sharp Hellinger–TV inequalities.	
Information/Testing/Hellinger/Regularity	Information/Testing/Hellinger/Regularity.tex	Scalar L² root differentiation, tangent condition, quadratic Hellinger coefficient, continuous L²-product map into L¹ and first-order TV coefficient.	
Notation correspondence
These are reader-facing aliases of Lean-owned definitions, not a second definition store. Exact result bindings live beside each TeX statement.
Paper notation	Lean identifier	
probe family 𝒫_C; continuation-probe family ℱ_C	ProbeFamily	
x ∼⁰_C y and x ≈_C y	indist F x y (the family instance selects the relation)	
f factors through q	Factors f q	
q sufficient for F_C	Sufficient F q	
coarsest quotient X_C / ≈_C	IndistQuot, toQuot, toQuot_sufficient, indist_of_sufficient	
family growth 𝒦₁ ⊆ 𝒦₂ (context form) and Γ₁ ⊆ Γ₂ (endpoint form)	ProbeFamily.extend, indist_mono	
jointly separating extensions	JointlySeparating	
the no-go obstruction	no_go	
pulled-back family f' ∘ e_*	ProbeFamily.pullback	
defect Δ(e, q)	InDefect, DefectEmpty, defectEmpty_iff_sufficient	
class split under an extension	extended_split, const_insufficient_after	
interventions Int_R(A, a)	Interv	
detectable intervention influence A ⇝_R B	Influences	
resource monotonicity from protocol inclusion	influences_mono	
the finite model without transitivity	influences_A_B, influences_B_C, not_influences_A_C	
covered extensions split no class	indist_pullback_of_factors	
detected loss is not recovered	no_recovery	
factorization is fiber constancy (surjective q)	factors_iff_fiber_const	
normalized total variation d_TV	Approximation.tv; tv_eq_eventTV proves the event formulation	
common-kernel simulation error e(K;E,F)	Approximation.simulationError	
directed deficiency δ_sim(E,F)	Approximation.deficiency	
bounded-loss risk R_E(D,ℓ;θ)	Approximation.risk	
mutual information I(ρ), in nats	Information.mutualInfo	
channel information I(μ,K) and capacity C(K;𝒜)	Information.channelInfo, Information.capacity	
expected-cost constraint ℬ_c,b	Information.costAdmissible	
optimal binary error e_π(P,Q)	Information.binaryError	
independent sample law P^{⊗n}	Information.iidLaw	
Chernoff coefficient Z_s(P,Q) and information ξ(P,Q)	Information.chernoffCoeff, Information.chernoffInfo	
common support S, log likelihood ℓ, weights w_s, continuous partition Z̄_s	Information.commonSupport, Information.logLikelihood, Information.supportWeight, Information.supportPartition	
tilted probability law R_s and sample sum S_n(f)	Information.tiltedLaw, Information.sampleSum	
normalized negative log error r_n	Information.binaryErrorRate	
event test on A and uniform interval law U_θ	Information.eventTest, Information.intervalLaw	
square-root density r, law P_r, affinity ρ, squared distance H²	Information.RootDensity, its law, affinity, and hellingerSq	
L² root derivative v at θ	Information.HasRootDerivAt	
L¹ density r² and product fg	Information.RootDensity.density, Information.l2Product	
Approximation and simulation
The approximation branch owns its probability/Markov interfaces, not a surrogate finite test metric. Its δ_sim is distinct from the observer profile's record-error tolerance, exact extension defect, decision regret, recovery error and repair cost. The chosen simulator is independent of the unknown parameter. Infimum-based risk transfer keeps an explicit positive tolerance; it does not assert an attained best simulator. The forward bound does not prove the converse randomization theorem or resource feasibility.
Information and channel capacity
The information branch reuses the same Markov-channel interface. Its KL and mutual information use natural logarithms and retain infinite values. The Rust ChannelCapacityNats value-holder uses the same natural-log units but stores only a supplied finite number; it is not the formal capacity functional. Values expressed in bits need conversion by multiplication by ln(2), and any projection still needs input-law provenance. The input theorem holds on arbitrary measurable carriers: the Likelihood child pulls back a joint density by testing each output event separately, without assuming a common null set for every event. Extended-valued relative entropy is preserved, including infinite values. The alternative standard-Borel disintegration proof remains mathematical conditioning, not an admitted recovery operation.
Binary testing
Binary testing uses mathlib's Bayes risk, an infimum over all Markov decision kernels, rather than defining optimality by the overlap formula. Its finite bound keeps the prior factor and derives repetition from product probability laws. Zero masses are allowed. Chernoff information uses the extended logarithm and an open exponent interval: disjoint supports give infinity, not the finite value produced by applying Real.log at zero. Coefficient bounds, identical-law and disjoint-support cases are proved. The full finite-alphabet asymptotic equality now follows from a matching lower bound and a logarithmic squeeze. The continuous common-support partition has endpoint values Q(S) and P(S), not necessarily one. Its attained minimum equals the original open-interval infimum. Directional optimality, rather than an assumed zero-mean tilt, handles boundary minimizers. The typical-set bound uses the actual product measure and an explicit variance budget. The limit requires both priors positive and fixed; no equal-prior or positive-point-mass restriction is imposed. Repeated-use coding and local-testing regularity remain separate obligations; this finite-alphabet proof is not a theorem for arbitrary observation spaces or sample-dependent priors.
Conditional laws and moving support
The separate Conditional child has no finite-alphabet assumption. A measurable restriction identity Q|A = Q(A) P determines actual Bayes risk; independent products multiply its likelihood factor. MovingSupport applies this to Lebesgue-uniform intervals, not counting-measure uniform laws. An alternative endpoint θ + h/n yields limiting error min(a, b exp(-h/θ)), with a strictly nontrivial balanced-prior limit for h > 0. This is a sample-dependent local alternative, not the fixed-alternative Chernoff theorem. It establishes a counterexample to a universal square-root sample scale, not the general quadratic-mean differentiability, LAN or KL-expansion theory.
Hellinger distance and regularity
The Hellinger branch uses an arbitrary common reference measure, not a finite alphabet. Nonnegative unit L² elements construct probability laws, and equal laws have equal roots in that L² space. Its half-squared-norm convention gives H² = 1 - ρ. The Variation child derives the density formula from the existing test/event TV definition and proves H² ≤ TV and TV² ≤ H²(2-H²). There is no second operational distance. The Regularity child owns scalar root differentiation: normalization implies ⟨r,v⟩ = 0, while Hellinger squared has coefficient ‖v‖₂²/2. The actual bounded product L² × L² → L¹ gives density derivative 2rv and TV coefficient ‖rv‖₁. No pointwise derivative is substituted for norm differentiability. These are single-observation, scalar-parameter results; product-law local testing, score/Fisher correspondence, LAN and KL expansion/failure claims are separate outstanding work. The common measure is fixed throughout these statements.
Encoding notes
Carriers are types. Probes have per-index codomains. Present and continuation-sensitive relations share one ProbeFamily representation. The no-go module absorbs each composite p ∘ e_* into a family member. Analytic results import mathlib instead of replacing real numbers, measures, integrals or topology with surrogate assumptions.
Use Unicode mathematical notation (→, ↦, ∀, ∃, ≤, ≠, ∘) in Lean and ordinary ASCII TeX commands in the paper. Match arms retain Lean's required => syntax. Input-method escape hints belong in the editor, not the mathematical source. Keep type/definition names and theorem names consistent with Lean conventions; do not rename public identifiers merely to simulate visual equality with a TeX symbol. Automatic implicit-variable creation is disabled for the library, so a misspelled or unimported symbol cannot silently become a fresh type parameter.
Documentation and refactoring
Follow mathlib's documentation and naming conventions. Module introductions identify the mathematical purpose, companion and any non-obvious encoding choice. Definition and major-theorem docstrings explain meaning and essential scope; they do not narrate tactics or repeat the paper. Use declaration references for dependencies and named TeX labels for results, not unstable theorem numbers. Keep terminology, parameter roles and assumptions consistent across related modules. Record necessary notation differences once at their owner; for example, weight denotes λ in the variational modules because Lean reserves the bare symbol.
A refactor moves ownership, not just text. Remove the old implementation or replace its exposition with a reference; update imports, bindings and callers together. Review both mathematical meaning and executable behavior after the move. Source synchronization must not leave two competing definitions or stale explanations. The PDF contains mathematical substance and research limits; maintenance policy and proof-coverage tracking stay in this guide and in coverage.toml, outside the typeset narrative.
Outstanding proof obligations

Every result used in a paper proof needs a proof in that module or a reference to the Lean declaration with the required hypotheses.
No sorry, assumed conclusion, custom axiom or unsafe proof substitute is acceptable. The axiom audit permits only Lean's standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Passing the paper build or the Lean build alone does not establish full correspondence or Rust implementation parity.

Each public type in kernel/src/ carries one rustdoc Lean:  line: a fully qualified declaration in backticks, or none. followed by the missing correspondence. Fields and associated methods use that type's reference and qualifications. The checker rejects absent or malformed lines and resolves all named declarations through the same Lean existence and axiom audit as the paper bindings.
A reference identifies the mathematical definition or result to compare. It does not prove that the Rust type implements it: an event identifier still needs a predicate, an intervention still needs its allowed transformation, the resource comparison does not prove protocol inclusion, and a finite grid is not a continuous optimiser. Types without a counterpart keep that gap explicit. The public-API tests in kernel/tests/ exercise numeric behaviour separately; the whole-paper and formal/kernel correspondence review remains open.

python3 check_correspondence.py

python3 check_correspondence.py --allow-open

Strict mode fails while any source-declared obligation remains open. The partial check permits open work only when the register and the included paper sources agree. Both modes still reject missing proof bindings, unresolved declarations and untrusted axioms.

MONAD Formal Mathematics
The Lean library defines MONAD’s mathematical objects and proves their properties. Use this guide to locate a definition, match paper notation to Lean, or maintain the library. The paper explains the same mathematics through one TeX companion per module.
lean-toolchain pins Lean 4; lakefile.toml pins mathlib to its matching v4.34.0 commit. lake-manifest.json records the transitive dependency revisions.
For a first encounter with the definitions, read a preservation claim in Lean. It carries a four-state example through ProbeFamily, Factors, Sufficient, the observational quotient and the compression obstruction. The product worked example supplies the mathematical interpretation without requiring Lean. The index below is for locating the exact branch after that orientation.
Organization and parity
Every mathematical module has the same relative path and stem in both trees:
formal/MonadFormal/Quotient.lean
paper/MonadFormal/Quotient.tex

Dependencies are imported, never reimplemented. General definitions live in Sandbox; specialized modules add hypotheses and reuse those definitions. The TeX companions carry leanproof and leandef bindings to fully qualified Lean declarations. The bindings do not add code identifiers to the typeset mathematics. Use stable result names and labels for references. The same rule applies below a module: Repair/Optimal.lean mirrors Repair/Optimal.tex, and Repair/Supplement.lean mirrors Repair/Supplement.tex. Parent modules own shared interfaces; children import them rather than restating their definitions.
The correspondence checker verifies both directions of the module/companion map, rejects duplicate inclusions and stale or duplicate public imports, and checks every displayed proof's binding, declaration resolution, trusted axiom dependencies, and local notation rules. It cannot infer that prose and Lean have identical hypotheses: that statement-level review remains mandatory. A theorem about finite states cannot discharge a measurable-space claim merely because its name matches.
Contents

Repair	Repair.tex	Adaptive feasibility, non-recovery and free-information bounds.

Temporal/Variational	Temporal/Variational.tex	Coercive Hilbert-space minimization, stationarity and exact energy gap.

Temporal/Variational/Paths	Temporal/Variational/Paths.tex	Exact correspondence with the full admissible H¹ path class; energy invariance and uniqueness of the minimizing path on [0,1].	
Temporal/Variational/Shift	Temporal/Variational/Shift.tex	Shifted-difference adjoint with separate forward/backward boundary supports and an L² force.	
Temporal/Variational/Regularity	Temporal/Variational/Regularity.tex	Mean-zero orthogonality, absolutely continuous integration by parts, and velocity regularity derived from the weak equation.	
Temporal/Variational/Euler	Temporal/Variational/Euler.tex	Nonlocal Euler equation for the unique minimizing path, with an absolutely continuous velocity and an L² second derivative almost everywhere.	
Information	Information.tex	KL mutual information on probability laws, measurable and Markov processing, single-letter capacity and admissible input costs.	
Information/Likelihood	Information/Likelihood.tex	Joint-density pullback and exact extended-valued relative-entropy transport on arbitrary measurable carriers, without disintegration.	
Information/Input	Information/Input.tex	General deterministic coarse-graining identity, capacity comparison, cost transport and measurable-section realizability; separate standard-Borel conditional-law reconstruction.	
Information/Testing	Information/Testing.tex	Actual Bayes-risk optimization over all randomized tests, with an attained likelihood-ratio rule and finite-alphabet overlap formula.	
Information/Testing/Chernoff	Information/Testing/Chernoff.tex	Prior-weighted finite-sample bound, independent-product tensorization, coefficient bounds and extended-valued information with exact support cases.	
Information/Testing/Tilted	Information/Testing/Tilted.tex	Actual common-support tilted laws, continuous endpoint extension, attained minimum, directional optimality and likelihood transport.	
Information/Testing/Sampling	Information/Testing/Sampling.tex	Product-law mean and variance, Chebyshev concentration and an explicit typical-set sample budget.

Information/Testing/Conditional	Information/Testing/Conditional.tex	Exact optimal risk from a restriction likelihood identity, on arbitrary measurable spaces, and independent-product transport.

body:
Getting started
Build the Rust kernel to use it from code, the Lean library to read or extend proofs, or the paper to read the mathematical exposition. Start from a local source checkout and run each block from the repository root. The subshell commands return you to that root when they finish.
For a first calculation, follow a first Rust call. For a first formal statement, build Lean below and continue with the preservation example.
Important

There is no released package. The Lean library and paper build from formal/ and paper/ in this repository. A mathematics, paper or kernel change needs all the checks below; a documentation-only change needs its examples and affected links checked.
The full check set needs four toolchains
Rust kernel
Install Rust with Cargo, Clippy and Rustfmt. The kernel has no external dependencies.
Lean library
Install Lean through elan. The versions in formal/lean-toolchain, formal/lakefile.toml and formal/lake-manifest.json keep Lean, mathlib and the other dependencies in step.
Correspondence checker
Install Python 3.11 or later and prepare the Lean environment. Use Python for the checker and its tests.
Paper
Install a TeX distribution with pdflatex and bibtex, plus Make and Bash. Install pdftotext to check the rendered text. The validator reports that check as skipped when the tool is missing.
Run the checked-in examples and build targets
make examples runs the Rust calculation and the Lean reading example. Use make example-rust or make example-lean for just one. The Lean target builds the pinned library first.
make check-formal builds Lean and runs the strict correspondence checker. It returns failure while the three registered obligation groups remain open; the target does not turn that refusal into success. make check-formal-partial runs the same build and the explicitly partial check. The individual commands and their meanings follow below.
make check-protos requires protoc and sibling source checkouts named MUON, HENA, Q-MUON and Q-HENA, and, when MONAD_PRIVATE_CONSUMERS names it, another consumer's checkout. Set that variable to a comma-separated list of sibling checkout names; the script's --help explains it. It compiles each header separately, including imports, and writes descriptors and compiler dependency files under the ignored target/proto-checks/ directory. Override SIBLING_ROOT if those checkouts are elsewhere, or PROTOC to select the compiler executable. Missing source directories fail before compilation.
Classical HENA uses MUON’s muon/unit.proto; Q-HENA uses Q-MUON’s copy of that same virtual path. Their include roots stay separate. The .d dependency files identify the physical compiler inputs: equal descriptors do not establish that the same source was read. These are header syntax and import checks, with unused-import warnings expected in message-free headers. They do not check a consumer’s runtime behaviour, pin a release’s source revisions or prove quantum compatibility. Reckon’s self-contained schemas are outside this MONAD-dependent check.
Build the Lean library
(cd formal && lake build)

The first build downloads mathlib and may take time. Later builds reuse its cache. A successful build means the Lean modules compile; the paper comparison is a separate check.
Check the paper against Lean
The correspondence checker pairs Lean modules with TeX companions and checks that every displayed proof names a real declaration. It also checks that the proofs depend only on the permitted axioms.
Run the partial check
(cd formal && python3 check_correspondence.py --allow-open)

This checks the module and proof bindings while allowing the open obligations in the coverage register.
Run the strict check
(cd formal && python3 check_correspondence.py)

The strict check runs the same checks and also fails while source-declared obligations remain open. Both modes require formal/coverage.toml to match the open-obligation comments in the included TeX sources; an emptied or inconsistent register fails. Strict failure on the three current groups is expected. Close an obligation in its source and register only when its proof or review is complete. The formal guide explains the markers and the limits of this check.
Test the checker
(cd formal && python3 -m unittest -v test_correspondence)

These tests check the checker’s behavior. Reviewing a paper statement still requires comparing its exact hypotheses and conclusion with Lean.
Test the kernel
Run the tests, lint and formatting check:
cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml -- --check

Build the paper
make check-paper-build tests the shared bibliography and figure recipe with small temporary papers. It requires Make, Python, pdflatex, bibtex and pdftotext. The bibliography tests check actual entries and rendered text, including citations in included chapters, stale output and errors that BibTeX reports with a successful exit. indexed.title: Getting started
indexed.body:
Getting started
Build the Rust kernel to use it from code, the Lean library to read or extend proofs, or the paper to read the mathematical exposition. Start from a local source checkout and run each block from the repository root. The subshell commands return you to that root when they finish.
For a first calculation, follow a first Rust call. For a first formal statement, build Lean below and continue with the preservation example.
Important

There is no released package. The Lean library and paper build from formal/ and paper/ in this repository. A mathematics, paper or kernel change needs all the checks below; a documentation-only change needs its examples and affected links checked.
The full check set needs four toolchains
Rust kernel
Install Rust with Cargo, Clippy and Rustfmt. The kernel has no external dependencies.
Lean library
Install Lean through elan. The versions in formal/lean-toolchain, formal/lakefile.toml and formal/lake-manifest.json keep Lean, mathlib and the other dependencies in step.
Correspondence checker
Install Python 3.11 or later and prepare the Lean environment. Use Python for the checker and its tests.
Paper
Install a TeX distribution with pdflatex and bibtex, plus Make and Bash. Install pdftotext to check the rendered text. The validator reports that check as skipped when the tool is missing.
Run the checked-in examples and build targets
make examples runs the Rust calculation and the Lean reading example. Use make example-rust or make example-lean for just one. The Lean target builds the pinned library first.
make check-formal builds Lean and runs the strict correspondence checker. It returns failure while the three registered obligation groups remain open; the target does not turn that refusal into success. make check-formal-partial runs the same build and the explicitly partial check. The individual commands and their meanings follow below.
make check-protos requires protoc and sibling source checkouts named MUON, HENA, Q-MUON and Q-HENA, and, when MONAD_PRIVATE_CONSUMERS names it, another consumer's checkout. Set that variable to a comma-separated list of sibling checkout names; the script's --help explains it. It compiles each header separately, including imports, and writes descriptors and compiler dependency files under the ignored target/proto-checks/ directory. Override SIBLING_ROOT if those checkouts are elsewhere, or PROTOC to select the compiler executable. Missing source directories fail before compilation.
Classical HENA uses MUON’s muon/unit.proto; Q-HENA uses Q-MUON’s copy of that same virtual path. Their include roots stay separate. The .d dependency files identify the physical compiler inputs: equal descriptors do not establish that the same source was read. These are header syntax and import checks, with unused-import warnings expected in message-free headers. They do not check a consumer’s runtime behaviour, pin a release’s source revisions or prove quantum compatibility. Reckon’s self-contained schemas are outside this MONAD-dependent check.
Build the Lean library
(cd formal && lake build)

The first build downloads mathlib and may take time. Later builds reuse its cache. A successful build means the Lean modules compile; the paper comparison is a separate check.
Check the paper against Lean
The correspondence checker pairs Lean modules with TeX companions and checks that every displayed proof names a real declaration. It also checks that the proofs depend only on the permitted axioms.
Run the partial check

This checks the module and proof bindings while allowing the open obligations in the coverage register.
Run the strict check
(cd formal && python3 check_correspondence.py)

Strict failure on the three current groups is expected. Close an obligation in its source and register only when its proof or review is complete. The formal guide explains the markers and the limits of this check.

These tests check the checker’s behavior. Reviewing a paper statement still requires comparing its exact hypotheses and conclusion with Lean.
Test the kernel
Run the tests, lint and formatting check:
cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml -- --check

body:
The kernel
monad-kernel provides Rust types for states, observers, resources and intervention records, plus numerical operations on finite probability distributions. The crate has no external dependencies and runs inside the caller’s process. It represents part of MONAD’s finite observer model; the Lean library defines the wider mathematics.
What the kernel types establish
The kernel stores numerical observations and metadata. Its types establish the following, with the stated limits:
DirectInfluenceRecords stores observed direct pairs. It does not check reflexivity or transitivity. The paper proves that detectable influence is not transitive in general.
ReliableRecord holds metadata for the paper's reliable record. Its method checks that the supplied error bound is finite and in [0, 1/2). It does not verify the decision rule, trials or persistence.
ChannelCapacityNats holds a finite value in nats per use that you supply. Multiply a value in bits by ln(2) before passing it. The Lean library defines capacity in nats as a noncomputable supremum over the declared admissible input laws. That definition is not an executable capacity estimator.
ResourceVector::fits_within checks that the receiver's coordinates are less than or equal to the argument's, including finite nonnegative epsilon values. The meaning and order of epsilon still need a profile; comparing fields establishes no inclusion of available protocols.
StateSpace::new stores a regulator and dimension without validating nonzero values or state indices. A stored cardinality bound does not construct dynamics, a measure or a proof that a consumer's states obey it.
The traits Evolution, CoarseGraining, RecordChannel and AllowedOps have no implementations. A consumer that implements them must establish the required laws. TotalVariation computes a finite-vector distance. ChernoffInformation uses a grid approximation without a certified numerical error bound; its error_probability_bound method does not provide a certified finite-sample guarantee.
Compare a type with its formal reference
Each public type's Rust documentation names a Lean declaration to compare or explains why it has no counterpart. The formal guide describes the checked Lean: lines. Running the correspondence checker resolves those names and audits their axioms; it does not prove that a numeric implementation satisfies the named definition or theorem.
The tests in kernel/tests/correspondence.rs compare total variation with all events on small finite carriers, check the Chernoff grid against independent decimal reference values, and compute the three-bit intervention model's cancelling effect. The xor example uses the zero preparation and the intervention functions in MonadFormal.model, MonadFormal.intA and MonadFormal.intB. It establishes behaviour for those inputs, not a general causal-identification result. The other kernel tests cover their own numerical domains and failure cases.
How to depend on it
Research systems clone MONAD beside their own repository and declare a Cargo path dependency on MONAD's kernel folder. The dependency name is monad-kernel. The crate is not published to a registry.
A first Rust call
You need Rust, Cargo and a local MONAD checkout. Lean, Python and TeX are needed only for the other checks in getting started.
The checked-in first-use example contains the calculation below. Run it from this repository with make example-rust, or follow the consumer setup to use the crate from a separate project.
Find MONAD/kernel/Cargo.toml in your checkout. Create monad-first-use beside the MONAD directory and create a src directory inside it. The consumer needs the two files below.
Declare the dependency
Create monad-first-use/Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "monad-first-use"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
monad-kernel = { path = "../MONAD/kernel" }

The path is relative to this manifest. Change it if your MONAD checkout is elsewhere. There is no registry release to use instead.
Compare two distributions
Create monad-first-use/src/main.rs. Both vectors describe the ordered outcomes [record absent, record present] under two hypothetical preparations. The example supplies these laws; the kernel does not measure or infer them.
use monad_kernel::causality::{
    CausalRelation, DetectabilityThreshold, Distinguishability, TotalVariation,
};

fn main() {
    let p = [0.8, 0.2];
    let q = [0.2, 0.8];
    let distance = TotalVariation.divergence(&p, &q);
    assert!((distance - 0.6).abs() < 1e-12);

    let observation = CausalRelation {
        cause: 0,
        effect: 1,
        distinguishability: distance,
        threshold: DetectabilityThreshold(0.9),
    };

    println!("total variation: {distance:.3}");
    println!("meets threshold: {}", observation.is_detected());
}

Run the calculation
From monad-first-use, run:
cargo run --offline

The result is:
total variation: 0.600
meets threshold: false

Total variation is half the sum of absolute coordinate differences: here (0.6 + 0.6) / 2 = 0.6. Equivalently, it is the largest difference the two laws assign to the same event. A threshold of 0.9 rejects this numerical observation; changing it to 0.5 makes the second line true. Neither result establishes that the laws came from valid matched interventions or reliable records. The event identifiers and threshold are metadata supplied by the caller.
Warning

Invalid probability vectors panic. Supply equal nonzero lengths, finite entries in [0, 1], and a total within 1e-10 of one for each vector. Keep the same outcome order in both. Validate external data before calling the API; raw counts need conversion into a justified probability model first.
If Cargo cannot find the kernel, check the dependency path relative to the consumer manifest. The kernel source lists its module exports; working on the mathematics explains the formal definitions and proof workflow.
The preservation-under-uncertainty explanation puts probabilistic comparison in the wider research question. For exact answer preservation, return to the summary example: its quotient and source-dependent repair are separate from the distance calculation here.
The kernel changes only by addition within a stage
Within a stage, changes add types, implementations, methods, and tests. They do not rename, remove, or change signatures.
Breaking changes happen only at a stage boundary. Every consumer must compile again before that boundary closes.
A new dependency is a contract change.
New trait implementations arrive with law tests. For example, an evolution must be bijective and measure-preserving.
The protocol buffers are headers until a consumer needs a message
protos/monad/ holds state.proto, observer.proto, and causality.proto. Each file is a header with no messages. Messages arrive when a cross-language consumer needs them. Each message will mirror a kernel type in name and shape.

body:
MONAD as a library
MONAD lets a caller use a limited executable part of its mathematics inside its own process. Research kernels already depend on monad-kernel; the wider language interfaces and visualisation tools described here are planned. The Lean library owns definitions and proofs, the paper explains them, and the Rust kernel supplies separately tested types and finite-distribution calculations.
Two kinds of consumer
Research repositories use kernel/ directly through a Cargo path dependency. Changing that shared API requires a coordinated migration and a build of every consumer, as the kernel guide explains.
Other tools will use one Rust facade, monad-sdk, directly or through a language interface. Each interface wraps or generates from that facade; it does not reimplement the mathematics. MONAD has no daemon, command line or service. A caller needing a service supplies its own adapter and decides who may use it. Protobuf definitions describe wire data, not a server.
One Rust facade, several language interfaces
Home	Intended use	
sdk/rust/	The complete, narrow Rust facade and its headless scene compiler, tested through the public API and conformance cases. Computation is effect-free.	
sdk/python/	A Rust extension through PyO3 and maturin, with generated Python type stubs, NumPy-native projections and step traces. It works with Manim without depending on it.	
sdk/js/	A native Node module through napi-rs for services and tooling.	
sdk/go/	A pure-Go decoder and validator for profile manifests and conformance records. It does not reproduce the kernel's calculations.	
sdk/wasm/	The full effect-free sandbox in the browser, avoiding a server round trip for its computations.	
sdk/viz/	React views of scene records.	
Each SDK is intended to become an independent repository. Its licence, notice and citation files arrive with its implementation. Directory names and the proposed Rust facade name reserve no package registry coordinates.
Framework integrations depend on those interfaces. integrations/torch/ supplies tensor wrappers over the Python SDK; integrations/hf/ supplies model-side wrappers over it. integrations/manim/ animates scene records using the Python SDK and an exactly pinned ManimCE release. The SDKs do not depend on these integrations.
Pictures read the same scene records
The Rust facade's headless compiler will emit typed scene records with stable cell identities and step traces for refinement, splits, merges and transport. Manim animations, React views and browser computations use that shared representation. Renderers read records; they originate no mathematical facts. TikZ remains the source of the paper's figures, and exploratory notebooks in notebooks/ illustrate results rather than establish them.
The five picture primitives express the following mathematical content. A scene must identify the definitions, assumptions or result it illustrates; an animation does not prove a programme-level claim.
Primitive	What it shows	
Class split	Generative openness: an equivalence cell divides when an extension admits a separating question.	
Quotient and refine	The exact quotient and monotonicity: merge states into the coarsest sufficient partition, then split cells when the admitted family grows.	
Transport flow	Invariant accounting: the preserved, hidden, collapsed and novel parts of one transformation.	
Path pair	Trajectory-sensitive relevance: two paths with the same endpoint can carry different relevance.	
No-go forcing	The compression obstruction: under the separating-extension assumptions, each proposed merge fails until the summary is injective.	
The scene contract must be available to its renderer before implementation. Calibration renders are internal evidence; publishing them is a separate decision. Causality's Manim animations, planned widgets and site imagery share this picture vocabulary. A shared visual language keeps the illustrated relationships consistent; each use still identifies the mathematics it actually illustrates.
Portable contracts wait for a second language
Bundle and hash machinery is deferred until a second language needs it. The intended arrangement is one canonical schema and a per-symbol profile map, generated into a portable profile bundle. A manifest in contracts/manifests/ would identify the corresponding paper section, Lean declaration and kernel symbol, with their source references and hashes. A private deterministic generator, proposed as crates/monad-contract-codegen, would write contracts/bundle/<profile>/; a proposed crates/monad-contracts crate would embed and validate it offline.
Each SDK would embed the same bundle and reject a mismatched profile hash. No SDK would copy a schema by hand. These checks establish which material a caller has, not mathematical equivalence: correspondence still needs the stated hypotheses, Lean proofs, executable tests and semantic review. Wire vocabulary stays in protos/.
contracts/conformance/ is the home for executable comparisons: direct pairs versus closure, cardinality, measure and entropy reference cases, and negative cases rejecting unsupported continuous or quantum interpretations. A sealed FORC 0.1 bundle would identify the historical profile, including its known divergences; it would not become the public API. No such bundle or suite exists yet.
Measure a defined update rule before accelerating it
SIMD and GPU work starts only after a well-posed compressed update rule exists with its invariant class declared. benchmarks/ measures error growth against horizon and cost against that class. Every benchmark states whether it tests trajectory fidelity or invariant statistics; those are different accuracy promises. kernel/gpu/cuda/ and kernel/gpu/mlx/ will hold the corresponding accelerated kernels.
What starts implementation and release
The finite observer profile is accepted as 0.2, with the detectability threshold and the interpretation of intervention influence still open. Acceptance does not supply an implemented SDK, symbol map or conformance suite. Those remain planned work; a second language's actual need comes before bundle machinery. A defined scene contract comes before renderers, and the update-rule condition above comes before acceleration. These conditions do not resume the paused calibration or further proving.
Package names and registry coordinates still need a decision and an availability check at that time. Publication posture also remains a separate decision; the bill of materials and publication quickstart follow it. The existing notice states current attribution, and the contributing guide and contributor agreement state the contribution terms. This design specifies where future code belongs and what it must preserve; it does not announce a package or a release.

body:
Working on the mathematics
Read a preservation claim by asking which questions the summary must still answer and which hypotheses the proof needs. Start with the four-state parts-and-fit example below. Calibration and further proving are paused.
Read a preservation claim in Lean
The four-state product example asks whether a part is available and fits a machine. Its state is a pair of Boolean values. Retaining availability alone merges two states with different repair answers. To express that issue in Lean, a ProbeFamily X supplies an index type I, an answer type O i for each question, and a function f i from the carrier X to that answer type. The answers need not all have the same type.
Build the pinned Lean environment first.
Define the example
The checked-in reading example imports the library and defines these inputs:
import MonadFormal.NoGo
import MonadFormal.Quotient

open MonadFormal

namespace ReadExample

abbrev PartState := Bool × Bool

def availability (x : PartState) : Bool := x.1
def repair (x : PartState) : Bool := x.1 && x.2

def repairFamily : ProbeFamily PartState where
  I := Unit
  O := fun _ ↦ Bool
  f := fun _ ↦ repair

#eval availability (true, false)
#eval availability (true, true)
#eval repair (true, false)
#eval repair (true, true)

#check @Factors
#check @Sufficient
#check @toQuot_sufficient
#check @quotient_universal
#check @no_go

end ReadExample

Inspect the definitions and results
From the repository root, run:
make example-lean

MONAD
MONAD studies what a description can tell apart and which distinctions survive compression or a change of description. Its Lean library defines and proves mathematical results. A paper explains them, and a small Rust kernel provides types and numerical operations for other research code.
Use the Rust kernel to compare finite observation laws from a local checkout. Use Lean to follow a proof or extend the formal library. Descriptions and repair and its four-state worked example explain the research without requiring a build. The name is short for Minimal Ontological Notions for Axiomatic Distinction. Category theory and programming languages use “monad” for a different concept.
MONAD has three surfaces
Lean owns the formal definitions and proofs. Each mathematical module has a matching TeX chapter, so the paper explains the same objects and results. The Rust kernel represents only part of a finite observer model. Its type names and operations need the interpretation in the kernel guide.
MONAD runs in a caller’s process. There is no daemon, CLI or service to start.
The mathematics is partly proved and nothing is published
The Lean library and paper share 42 mathematical modules. The correspondence checker links 82 displayed proofs to Lean declarations. body:
MONAD: Minimal Ontological Notions for Axiomatic Distinction
MONAD is the mathematics of Causality, whose unit and swarm kernels, MUON and HENA, compile against it. It is a mathematical research programme with an executable kernel, and it asks how a mathematical system can define, compress, transport, and revise its own space of distinctions when future continuations, historical trajectories, and transformations can change what is distinguishable.
For example, a description can compress two states into one because no admitted test separates them. A later extension can then require exactly that lost distinction. One checked obstruction makes the tradeoff precise: if the permitted questions separate every pair of states, preserving every answer exactly forces the summary to keep every distinct state apart. No nontrivial merging remains possible under those assumptions.
The repository has three surfaces. A Lean 4 library owns the formal definitions and proofs. A LaTeX paper explains the same mathematics, module by module. A Rust crate, monad-kernel, holds typed formal objects that sibling research systems use as a shared vocabulary.
Important

MONAD 0.1.0 is the paper and the Lean library. Calibration and further proving are paused. No package is published and no language SDK exists; research code uses kernel/ directly.
Use MONAD for a typed vocabulary or for the research itself
Use MONAD when you need a typed, dependency-free vocabulary for state spaces, observers, resource-indexed distinguishability, and causal records, or when you work on the research programme itself.
MONAD is a library and a body of mathematics. It runs inside a consumer’s process, with no daemon, command-line tool or service to start.
Start with the surface you need
For mathematical understanding, Descriptions and repair introduces the programme and What a summary preserves works through a finite compression and repair example. The name MONAD is unrelated to the programming-language or category-theoretic use of “monad”.
For a local source checkout, Getting started owns the toolchain prerequisites and build commands. The kernel carries a Rust consumer through a finite-distribution calculation. Working on the mathematics translates the product example into the existing Lean definitions and explains the quotient and obstruction hypotheses. The Lean library and the paper are in formal/ and paper/, and their instructions are in the formal guide.
Changes to the mathematics, paper or kernel require the full checks in that setup guide. A passing Lean build checks formal proofs; the correspondence checker links paper proofs to declarations and separately refuses full coverage while obligations remain. Neither check establishes that an executable consumer implements the entire mathematics.
Lean owns the mathematics and every other surface projects it
Surface	What a developer works with	
Lean library	Definitions, theorems and their exact hypotheses	
Paper	Mathematical explanations paired with the Lean modules	
Rust kernel	Shared types and implemented finite-distribution calculations	
Planned SDKs and integrations	Language interfaces and renderers over one Rust facade; nothing is implemented, and each folder holds only a note on what it will be	
Research kernels use kernel/ directly. The planned language interfaces share one Rust facade, and renderers read the scene records it produces. The library design owns that arrangement, the five picture primitives and the prerequisites for SDKs, portable contracts and GPU work.
Many results are proved and three groups remain open
The Lean library and the paper share 42 mirrored modules. Checked results include exact quotients and refinement, residual-budget continuation laws, partition abstraction, adaptive repair feasibility and optimal cost, exact supplement coding, statistical simulation and bounded-risk transfer, temporal elimination and a mixed-boundary resonance obstruction, a nonlocal variational construction with a strong Euler equation almost everywhere, finite influence counterexamples, measure-theoretic entropy conservation, mutual-information processing and capacity transport on arbitrary measurable spaces, the full finite-alphabet Chernoff exponent, a moving-support counterexample, and scalar Hellinger and total-variation coefficients.
Three groups of obligations are open: operational coding and local testing, quantum correspondence, and a statement-level review of the whole paper. formal/coverage.toml lists them, and the formal guide explains the strict check.
The kernel checks only some properties of its types. Read their guarantees and limits before using them. The successor profile, contract bundles, SDKs, integrations and GPU paths have no implementations.
Reuse comes before invention
Solve the stated problem by reuse, translation, composition, extension and, only when necessary, invention. A complete reduction to existing mathematics is a successful outcome. Compare explicit signatures and assumptions, not metaphors. Classify a mismatch as a definition, a conjecture, a theorem target, or a counterexample. Keep equivalence and identity apart. Keep mathematical representation and operational access apart. Keep inaccessible and destroyed information apart. Do not hide unresolved structure in a score.
The formal guide holds the documentation, notation, and refactoring conventions.
MONAD is the root of the Causality research stack
The research moves from MONAD's axioms to MUON's adaptive unit, Reckon's records and HENA's swarm. The table distinguishes direct code dependencies from the formal definitions used by Reckon’s manual.
Project	Relationship	
MUON	Consumer: the single unit	
Reckon	Formal definitions used by the laboratory manual; no current kernel dependency	
HENA	Consumer: swarm composition	
Q-MUON	Consumer: quantum unit fork	
Q-HENA	Consumer: quantum swarm fork	
Other downstream research projects	Consumers; this manual gives no integration guide for them	
MONAD is part of Causality, the research brand of RawThoughts Enterprises Private Limited, at causality.in.
MONAD is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later
MONAD's kernel, Lean formalization and paper use AGPL-3.0-or-later. The Lean formalization builds on the pinned Lean 4 toolchain and mathlib (Apache-2.0); those and other third-party material keep their own terms and required notices.
Commercial use is permitted under the applicable licence. Alternative terms require a separate written agreement with RawThoughts Enterprises Private Limited, which can grant them only for material it is entitled to relicense; this repository grants none. See NOTICE for ownership and the dependency statements, CITATION.cff for citation and CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution requirements. Outside contributions remain closed pending review of the draft agreement and a way to record acceptance.

body:
Resource admission and slot conformance
These are the proposed records and tests for MUON’s version-0 unit interface. No unit coordinator or adapter implements them. The first stock implementation can use today's kernel types; MONAD's mathematical research remains paused. The developer overview explains the five surfaces and capability report, with worked examples of quantity and error comparisons.
The caller, estimator, unit and allocator have different responsibilities. Admission checks whether a request is eligible; a reservation allocates capacity to a particular attempt. Keep both decisions explicit before inference. Define the caller-requirement, estimated-demand, fixed-capacity and admission-decision schemas with the first typed unit interface. Define availability and reservation records with the first shared pool, whether HENA or a standalone unit coordinator owns it, as described in HENA's design.
Admission needs five records written by different parties
A single bare resource vector, or one request written by whoever estimates the cost, cannot keep callers, estimators and allocators honest. Admission uses five records instead:
CallerRequirementsV1, signed by the caller or by the swarm's coordination: the input and parameter digests, the maximum tolerated error, the required fidelity and determinism, a deadline or latency class, and the caller's resource and cost ceilings.
EstimatedResourceDemandV1, from estimate_demand(input, params, capability_profile_ref): the estimator version, the unit and configuration identity, projected slots, bytes, tokens and energy, the estimate's confidence or upper-bound policy, and how long it is valid. It has no error-tolerance field, so an estimate can never write, relax or replace the caller's tolerance; it may report expected error only as labelled diagnostic evidence.
ResourceCapacityProfileV1, for one exact unit and configuration: its fixed capacity ceilings and the maximum error, fidelity, determinism and latency it guarantees. It never carries what is free right now.
ResourceAvailabilitySnapshotV1, issued by HENA's or the standalone unit coordinator's allocator: the current unreserved capacity and its generation and validity.
ResourceReservationV1, issued atomically by that allocator: capacity reserved for this holder and attempt against one live generation. The allocator design owns both records' complete fields and transitions.
Quantities are admitted the ordinary way: demand must be within the unreserved quantity, the capacity ceiling and the caller's ceiling, for slots, bytes, tokens and every admitted energy or cost dimension. Accuracy is a guarantee, not an amount, so its rule runs the other way: the unit's maximum error must be within the caller's tolerance, alongside the required fidelity, determinism and deadline. Anything missing, negative, non-finite, expired, mismatched or unversioned fails.
admit(caller_requirements, estimated_demand, capacity_profile, availability_snapshot) returns a ResourceAdmissionDecisionV1 that records all four references, the component-by-component result and the first constraint that failed. The decision establishes eligibility; the caller schedules only after the allocator issues a matching live reservation. The allocator design specifies atomic reservation, replay, expiry and recovery; the unit checks the resulting reservation before accepting the attempt.
Important

A unit refuses work without both a positive decision and a live matching reservation, with a typed error, never by silently degrading or truncating.
MONAD's current ResourceVector is only a compatibility carrier until MONAD settles what its epsilon means. An adapter may map it into these records only through an explicit, versioned mapping with tests, and no caller may treat its componentwise comparison as admission.
Conformance is a test suite
Conformance is a suite run per implementation and per stage, not a review judgment. It checks:
Completeness: all five surfaces callable, and the report accurate against observed behaviour (declared determinism reproduces, declared fidelity is delivered).
Identity: every report field is bound, and changing any of them changes the digest.
Resource algebra and authorship: equality and every single-component failure across the four admission inputs; quantity and error orders tested separately; the estimator unable to set or relax tolerance; bad identity, expiry, malformed and non-finite inputs failing closed; admission deterministic across language bindings.
Reservation safety: check stale release, renewal and consumption against the exact allocator generation, holder and attempt. Exact replay is idempotent and changed reuse conflicts. Concurrent reservations cannot oversubscribe. Crash, restart and double consumption must leave one allocator head and consistent accounting.
The compatibility vector: any mapping from MONAD's resource vector names its reading of epsilon and its version, proved by golden tests, and its comparison is never used as admission.
Budget honesty: a typed refusal without a decision and a live reservation; never silent truncation.
Observer floor: at least one binding emits well-ordered records that a Reckon-protocol store accepts in a harness run.
Checkpoint round-trip: checkpoint and restore give an identical report and conformant behaviour.
Opacity: one consumer drives two distinct implementations (two adapter backends at the stock stack; an adapter and the first micro-transformer unit at the first swap) through the contract alone, with no backend branches. Different capabilities and measured outputs are allowed; task adequacy and substitution need their own preregistered tests.
Version: the version is declared, and additive-only change is verified by diffing against the stage's baseline schema.
The stock stack exits for this contract when the suite exists, at least two adapters pass it, and the contract is stamped version 1. Until then every interface above is a design and may change without ceremony.
The training and evaluation procedure governs comparisons of task adequacy and replacement candidates. A passing interface test does not establish either claim.
Return to the developer overview.

EstimatedResourceDemandV1, from estimate_demand(input, params, capability_profile_ref): the estimator version, the unit and configuration identity, projected slots, bytes, tokens and energy, the estimate's confidence or upper-bound policy, and how long it is valid. It has no error-tolerance field, so an estimate can never write, relax or replace the caller's tolerance; it may report expected error only as labelled diagnostic evidence.
ResourceCapacityProfileV1, for one exact unit and configuration: its fixed capacity ceilings and the maximum error, fidelity, determinism and latency it guarantees. It never carries what is free right now.
ResourceAvailabilitySnapshotV1, issued by HENA's or the standalone unit coordinator's allocator: the current unreserved capacity and its generation and validity.
ResourceReservationV1, issued atomically by that allocator: capacity reserved for this holder and attempt against one live generation. The allocator design owns both records' complete fields and transitions.
Quantities are admitted the ordinary way: demand must be within the unreserved quantity, the capacity ceiling and the caller's ceiling, for slots, bytes, tokens and every admitted energy or cost dimension. Accuracy is a guarantee, not an amount, so its rule runs the other way: the unit's maximum error must be within the caller's tolerance, alongside the required fidelity, determinism and deadline. Anything missing, negative, non-finite, expired, mismatched or unversioned fails.
admit(caller_requirements, estimated_demand, capacity_profile, availability_snapshot) returns a ResourceAdmissionDecisionV1 that records all four references, the component-by-component result and the first constraint that failed. The decision establishes eligibility; the caller schedules only after the allocator issues a matching live reservation. The allocator design specifies atomic reservation, replay, expiry and recovery; the unit checks the resulting reservation before accepting the attempt.
Important

A unit refuses work without both a positive decision and a live matching reservation, with a typed error, never by silently degrading or truncating.
MONAD's current ResourceVector is only a compatibility carrier until MONAD settles what its epsilon means. An adapter may map it into these records only through an explicit, versioned mapping with tests, and no caller may treat its componentwise comparison as admission.
Conformance is a test suite
Conformance is a suite run per implementation and per stage, not a review judgment. It checks:
Completeness: all five surfaces callable, and the report accurate against observed behaviour (declared determinism reproduces, declared fidelity is delivered).
Identity: every report field is bound, and changing any of them changes the digest.
Resource algebra and authorship: equality and every single-component failure across the four admission inputs; quantity and error orders tested separately; the estimator unable to set or relax tolerance; bad identity, expiry, malformed and non-finite inputs failing closed; admission deterministic across language bindings.
Reservation safety: check stale release, renewal and consumption against the exact allocator generation, holder and attempt. Exact replay is idempotent and changed reuse conflicts. Concurrent reservations cannot oversubscribe. Crash, restart and double consumption must leave one allocator head and consistent accounting.
The compatibility vector: any mapping from MONAD's resource vector names its reading of epsilon and its version, proved by golden tests, and its comparison is never used as admission.
Budget honesty: a typed refusal without a decision and a live reservation; never silent truncation.
Observer floor: at least one binding emits well-ordered records that a Reckon-protocol store accepts in a harness run.
Checkpoint round-trip: checkpoint and restore give an identical report and conformant behaviour.
Opacity: one consumer drives two distinct implementations (two adapter backends at the stock stack; an adapter and the first micro-transformer unit at the first swap) through the contract alone, with no backend branches. Different capabilities and measured outputs are allowed; task adequacy and substitution need their own preregistered tests.
Version: the version is declared, and additive-only change is verified by diffing against the stage's baseline schema.
The stock stack exits for this contract when the suite exists, at least two adapters pass it, and the contract is stamped version 1. Until then every interface above is a design and may change without ceremony.
The training and evaluation procedure governs comparisons of task adequacy and replacement candidates. A passing interface test does not establish either claim.
Return to the developer overview.

body:
Building
Compile MUON’s muon-kernel crate or build its draft paper locally. The kernel uses MONAD’s crate, which Cargo fetches from MONAD’s repository at the commit the kernel manifest pins. The paper builds from its own copies of MONAD’s and MUON’s definitions in paper/shared/, so neither build needs another checkout.
Check the kernel
Use Rust and Cargo. From the MUON repository root:
Make sure Cargo can reach GitHub. The first check fetches monad-kernel at the pinned commit; later checks reuse Cargo’s copy, and --offline works once it is cached.
Compile the kernel crate:
cargo check --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml

Cargo should finish the dev profile after checking monad-kernel and muon-kernel. The latter re-exports the former. The command checks that the two crates compile together.
Build the paper
Install Make, Bash and a TeX distribution providing pdflatex and bibtex. Use pdftotext to inspect the rendered text as well as opening the PDF.
From MUON’s repository root, run:
make -C paper all

Open paper/MUON.pdf and check the text. The master imports MUON’s definitions and MONAD’s. If TeX reports a missing definitions file, check that paper/shared/monad/definitions.tex exists. This build uses only those two sets of shared definitions.
The research statement defines the proposed unit and its comparisons; it reports no working implementation or experiment. A PDF build checks typesetting, not the proposed unit’s behavior. Review missing-reference warnings and check that the rendered definitions and mathematical symbols are readable.
Return to the unit interface to understand what a future implementation would need to provide.

body:
MUON
A caller that swaps one model for another needs the same calls from both. MUON (Micro-Unit Operating Network) specifies those calls: what a model adapter has to report, what it can expose about its state, and when it refuses a request. HENA studies how several units would work together through those calls.
Important

The interface is a design. The muon-kernel crate re-exports MONAD’s kernel. The draft v0 contract below has no unit coordinator or adapter implementation. The first stock implementation can use today's kernel types without waiting for MONAD's paused mathematical research.
Build the kernel crate and the paper
Compile the type re-export and, optionally, the paper stating the proposed research.
Understand the reasoning problem
Follow a road notice into the next route answer and see how different units would be compared.
A unit is anything that fills the slot
The slot is the common interface a caller would use. An adapter would translate these five sets of calls to a model backend.
Each unit would have its own state space and an observer interface pairing MONAD coarse-grainings with record channels. A coarse-graining specifies the view of state an observer can distinguish; the channel carries the resulting records to a store maintained by its owner. A declared view need not expose the model's complete internal state.
Inference. Answer a request in one shot or as a stream, with explicit sampling parameters and seed behavior.
State. Describe the state space and expose a snapshot at a declared fidelity: an opaque checkpoint, a summary such as cache occupancy, or typed internal state. A backend that can expose only a summary must say so.
Observers. Emit records ordered by episode, step and sequence, with input and output digests and resource use. A store can retain those records independently; the unit does not decide its retention policy.
Budgets. Estimate demand and refuse work without an admissible request and a live matching reservation. Silent truncation would change the work the caller asked for.
Lifecycle. Initialize, participate in a caller-driven loop, checkpoint, restore and shut down. Checkpoint fidelity is explicit, so a caller knows what can be recovered.
Contract and capability
A capability report identifies the model revision, tokenizer, quantization, backend, runtime and device, along with supported inputs, streaming, state fidelity and checkpoint behavior. Record whether the configuration requests deterministic behavior and whether repeated runs have shown it. A change to any field that defines the unit changes its identity.
The report describes fixed capacity and supported behavior. Free capacity changes as work reserves or releases it, so it belongs to the allocator used by the standalone unit coordinator or HENA.
When choosing an adapter, check the operations and fidelity in its capability report. If it exposes only cache occupancy, a caller that needs typed state must choose a different one. Two units that meet the interface can still return different answers or have different costs. Use a task comparison before replacing one.
Admission and reservation answer different questions
Before inference, the caller states the required fidelity, tolerated error, deadline and resource ceilings. The estimator calculates demand for the given input, unit and configuration. The unit's capacity profile states what it can guarantee. The allocator reports what is still free and when that observation expires. The admission decision checks those four inputs together.
Consider an illustrative token budget, with all other constraints already satisfied:
Input	Value	
Caller ceiling	500 tokens	
Estimated demand	150 tokens	
Unit capacity	1,000 tokens	
Unreserved quantity in the current snapshot	200 tokens	
The request fits all three ceilings. Suppose two requests both pass against the same snapshot. The allocator reserves 150 tokens for the first request in one atomic update. Only 50 tokens remain, so the second cannot reserve 150 from the same pool. Start work only after both a positive admission decision and a matching live reservation.
Accuracy uses a different comparison. If the caller tolerates error up to 0.05, a guaranteed maximum error of 0.02 fits; a guarantee of 0.08 does not. Error tolerance is not a quantity to reserve, and the estimator cannot relax it to make a request fit.
A unit must refuse an expired or mismatched reservation rather than continuing under an old allocation. HENA's allocator design keeps the holder, work and generation identities, lease transitions and recovery cases together. Those records are defined with the first shared pool; they prevent concurrent callers from spending the same capacity and identify the allocation an interrupted request held.
Before mapping MONAD's compatibility ResourceVector into these records, define the meaning and ordering of the legacy epsilon coordinate and version that mapping. Do not interpret epsilon as a maximum-error guarantee without that definition. Comparing two vectors cannot authorise a run.
Stock models fill the slot first
The plan starts with adapters for stock open-weight models. The candidates are MLX on Apple Silicon, GGUF with llama.cpp and Ollama, and Hugging Face Transformers. The long-term design is a micro-transformer unit. It must meet the same interface and pass a comparison fixed in advance, at matched cost, between many identical units, one stronger unit, a mixture of units and no swarm. Coordination costs count, and every arm must meet the minimum performance for the task. If the small units lose, the strongest single or mixed implementation can keep using the same interface.
How experience can change a unit follows a notice through the current answer, the record store, learning across tasks and a possible change to the unit’s structure. The current re-export crate implements none of those mechanisms.
The training and evaluation procedure specifies the future harness's data manifests, matched comparisons, checkpoint records and separate release and activation steps. It opens no research stage.
The repository overview links the related projects and licence.

body:
MUON: Micro-Unit Operating Network
A reasoning system made of many small units needs each unit to say what it can do, what it will refuse and what it costs, so that one unit can stand in for another and the swap can be judged. MUON is the single-unit layer of Causality, the research programme that RawThoughts Enterprises Private Limited (RTEPL) runs at causality.in, with Harsh Joshi as author. MUON owns everything about one unit: the slot contract that every unit must honour, the models that fill the slot, and learning inside the unit. The plan starts with adapters for open-weight models and keeps a micro-transformer unit as the long-term implementation. HENA studies the swarm of many units. The formal types come from MONAD.
A unit that combines temporal processing with routed experts must give the temporal output a direct path to predictions, not only a say in which expert is selected. The research statement sets the comparison such a design must pass.
The muon-kernel crate re-exports MONAD
Today the repository holds the draft slot contract in docs/, the research statement, which sets out the proposed unit, its interface and the comparisons it must pass, and the muon-kernel crate, which only re-exports MONAD's kernel. protos/muon/unit.proto imports MONAD's state proto and declares no messages. No unit coordinator or adapter exists: a conformance suite, then adapters for open-weight models, are the problems in front of it.
The kernel builds on MONAD
The build guide gives the pinned MONAD dependency, kernel check and paper prerequisites. The developer overview explains the proposed slot, capabilities and resource admission. For the adaptive-unit question and learning examples, read Computation, state and learning.
MUON sits between MONAD and HENA
The research layers are MONAD (calculus) → MUON (one unit) → HENA (many units). Reckon is not the swarm's memory owner.
Repository	Relationship	
MONAD	The calculus; MUON's only code dependency	
HENA	The swarm, which depends on MUON's kernel	
Reckon	Measures whether a change helped, over records in stores their owners maintain; no code edge with MUON	
Q-MUON	The quantum variant, which keeps MUON's slot contract and is kept in step with MUON by merge at each stage	
MUON is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later
MUON's kernel, protocol header and paper use AGPL-3.0-or-later. Third-party material keeps its own terms and required notices.
Commercial use is permitted under the applicable licence. Alternative terms require a separate written agreement with RawThoughts Enterprises Private Limited, which can grant them only for material it is entitled to relicense; this repository grants none. See NOTICE for ownership, CITATION.cff for citation and CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution requirements. Outside contributions remain closed pending review of the draft agreement and a way to record acceptance.
