max_abs_stored_ablation_delta	Largest absolute finite stored ablation_delta.	
mean_stored_ablation_delta	Signed mean of finite stored ablation_delta values.	
Missing positive denominators or finite scores leave the affected field unavailable. A retrieval fraction cannot stand in for cue retention, and a stored delta needs its original experiment before it can support a claim about contribution.
Distinguish proxy-only records
Reports must flag a record as proxy-only when influence_proxy is present and both ablation_delta and counterfactual_delta are absent. A stored zero or negative delta is still present; a record with all three fields absent has no supplied attribution score. Preserve those distinctions when reporting record counts or interpreting a retention decision. Field presence describes the supplied score, while the original experiment establishes whether it is a valid measurement.
CausalScore.is_proxy_only computes the flag from those supplied fields. RecordSummaryMetrics.from_cmm() reports sorted proxy_only_record_ids and proxy_only_record_count for the current store without draining its event log. An examined empty store reports an empty list and zero; a summary constructed without an inventory leaves both unavailable. The flag is computed, so record serialization keeps the original score fields and their missing values without adding a wire field.
The debugger inspector labels each selected record’s supplied attribution source and counts proxy-only records in the selected event’s snapshot. Missing snapshots or score objects remain explicitly unavailable or incomplete. The experiment runner’s retention_score_source describes a whole run, and the graph’s measured, inferred and proxy edge labels describe relationships; neither replaces this record-by-record inventory. None of these reporting fields changes retention or validates a measurement.
What a contribution measurement should establish
The proposed record-contribution protocol asks whether removing a record or replacing it with random or null content, under the same budget and policy, causes a statistically significant performance drop at least as large as a declared threshold. Define the outcome, intervention, trial seeds and minimum useful difference before running it. The targets are:
Target	Meaning	
Causal precision	Fraction of stored records meeting that positive-usefulness test.	
Causal recall	Fraction of ground-truth necessary records retained.	
Counterfactual sensitivity	Outcome difference under the specified replacement or removal.	
Useful memory rate	Fraction of stored items retrieved and shown to affect a decision. Access counts alone do not establish that effect.	
Only measured ablation_delta or counterfactual_delta values can supply intervention evidence; report influence_proxy separately. An identified causal effect also needs a declared estimand, identification assumptions, negative controls, repeated runs and an uncertainty interval. A metric name, the ABLATION credit policy, matched seeds or a p-value cannot supply those conditions.
The working evaluator below implements one removal test. Its aggregate denominators differ from these proposed whole-store targets, and replacement remains unsupported.
Evaluation Protocol
CausalRecordEvaluator in src/reckon/metrics/evaluator.py runs paired task invocations with one actual record removal. Its defaults are 10 trials, an absolute delta threshold of 0.05 in the outcome’s units and alpha 0.05; the delta is not divided by the baseline. Trial independence still depends on the experiment. The procedure is:
Setup: Fix the task configuration, policy, budget, seed set and episodes per arm. Factories must return fresh instances. The evaluator snapshots declared task configuration, every budget field and policy configuration, then checks each arm against that snapshot. Tasks must derive their randomness from the supplied seed.
Select the record: An exact ID is accepted when it exists in both runs. For task-created records with fresh UUIDs, pass record_selector and use record_id as a stable report label. At the first read whose candidates match, the selector must identify exactly one record; multiple matches or a target that never reaches a read fail the evaluation.
Apply the intervention: The baseline retains the candidate. The other arm calls prune before access, logging or credit assignment, checks its success and verifies that the record is absent. The read then resolves again, so a ranked query can return its next candidate. An explicit-ID read returns no match for the removed ID.
Verify the pair: Both arms must reach the same read ordinal with matching selected payload, creation step, episode, cost, tags, source operation, utility, measured scores and metadata. Their digest excludes generated UUIDs and provenance input IDs; the selector supplies logical identity. A mismatch raises instead of returning a result. The report retains seeds, episodes per arm, both actual IDs, the shared target digest, removal status and both outcomes.
Measure the difference: Delta is baseline mean minus intervention mean, using a finite outcome where higher is better. A paired two-sided permutation test enumerates sign patterns up to 10,000; larger sets use 10,000 seeded draws. is_significant requires both the configured absolute effect threshold and p < alpha. is_useful additionally requires a strictly positive delta at or above the threshold.
Only ABLATE executes. MASK and REPLACE raise before task execution; their enum values do not imply support. The intervention removes one record instance at its first eligible read. A later replacement record is allowed, so this does not measure permanent suppression of the same fact. All four built-in tasks support this read-boundary intervention. Tutor reuses successful hints across episodes, so its comparison needs at least two episodes per arm; a one-episode run with no eligible record fails explicitly.
For example, evaluate a task-created key without pretending its UUID survives a fresh run:
from reckon.core.resources import MemoryBudget
from reckon.memory.manager import CausalMemoryManager
from reckon.metrics import CausalRecordEvaluator
from reckon.tasks import KeyDoorTask

evaluator = CausalRecordEvaluator(
    KeyDoorTask,
    lambda: CausalMemoryManager(MemoryBudget(max_slots=16)),
    lambda result: result.performance.success_rate,
    n_trials=10,
)
result = evaluator.evaluate_record(
    "first key", record_selector=lambda record: "key" in record.tags
)

The report preserves per-record deltas, trial counts and permutation p-values. It does not compute per-record confidence intervals. contract_precision is the fraction of distinct evaluated target labels with is_useful=True, using zero when none are evaluated. With non-empty ground-truth labels, contract_recall is the useful overlap divided by that set’s size; absent or empty ground truth leaves recall unavailable. Harmful and zero effects remain in the signed results but enter neither numerator. These descriptive aggregates use unadjusted per-record tests and establish neither family-wise error nor false-discovery control.
Supply your own paired runner
The separate Prober calls run_fn(ablated_ids, seed) twice per trial: ([], seed) for the baseline and ([record_id], seed) for removal. Each arm must start from the same task state; the caller owns removing the requested record after setup and before its use. Both arms must execute; precomputed unmatched baselines are refused. Replacement and shuffle requests raise before the runner is called. probe_episodes counts both arms, probe_wall_time_s measures the entire probe including statistics, and the returned configuration includes the actual first seed when one was generated.
Tests and intervals use the paired differences. The permutation test swaps labels within pairs (paired permutation design); it enumerates all sign patterns when they fit the configured resample count and otherwise samples them. The t-test is a one-sample test of differences against zero, equivalent to the paired t-test. Bootstrap resamples differences and centers its null draws at zero. Intervals are normal approximations for permutation, Student-t for t-tests and percentile bootstrap for bootstrap. Their assumptions and finite-sample limits still apply; a matched seed alone does not identify causation.
Fixed sampling uses n_trials pairs. Adaptive sampling applies only when both adaptive_sampling and early_stopping are true; otherwise the run uses n_trials. Adaptive sampling checks at min_trials, successive doublings, n_trials clipped to the allowed range, and max_trials. It stops for a significant difference or an interval wholly within ±delta_threshold; otherwise it reaches the maximum. Before the across-record correction, p-values are multiplied by the number of scheduled looks and intervals use alpha / looks. This Bonferroni adjustment covers the planned repeated looks subject to each test’s assumptions; the approximate intervals are not exact confidence sequences. Evidence.p_value is therefore the look-adjusted value, while p_value_adjusted additionally applies the configured correction across records. Benjamini–Hochberg assumes independence or the appropriate positive dependence across tests; shared seeds do not establish that assumption. Choose Bonferroni when arbitrary dependence must be covered. Both significance flags are two-sided; usefulness still requires the signed outcome comparison. The debugger graph displays supplied evidence and does not execute these probes.
Measure outcomes; do not optimise against a judge
Use the task outcome to test whether a record helped. A model's opinion that a record looks useful can be a labelled input, but should not replace the measured outcome. Validate a changed policy on held-out evidence before using it.
Diagnostic goals
Time to diagnose a failure is a qualitative measure in early versions. A later diagnostic comparison should also count which failures it can detect automatically: a missing cue, wrong retrieval, budget waste or drift. These are evaluation goals, not fields computed by the helpers above.
Probe Cost Accounting
Report task and probe episodes together, with their full elapsed time. ProbeCostTracker measures the bracketed probe time; the caller supplies base costs and records calls, episode counts, environment steps and evaluated records. A tracking label does not execute an intervention or establish its benefit.
Probe Cost Metrics
Metric	Description	Unit	
probe_episodes_total	Total episodes used for probing	count	
probe_wall_time_total_ms	Total wall time for all probes	milliseconds	
probe_calls_total	Total task.run invocations for probing	count	
probe_env_steps_total	Total environment steps for probing	count	
probe_records_evaluated	Number of records evaluated	count	
probe_episodes_per_record	Average episodes per record	episodes/record	
probe_wall_time_per_record_ms	Average wall time per record	ms/record	
probe_overhead_ratio	probe_time / (base_time + probe_time)	ratio (0-1)	
ProbeCostSummary aggregates these measurements. Per-record averages use zero when no records were evaluated; the overhead ratio uses zero when total elapsed time is zero.
Efficiency Metrics
EfficiencyMetrics.compute combines supplied reward, utility improvement and the recorded costs. Missing positive denominators produce zero. These ratios help compare costs; the caller still has to measure any claimed improvement.
Metric	Formula	Interpretation	
reward_per_total_episode	reward / (base_episodes + probe_episodes)	Performance accounting for all compute	
reward_per_total_wall_time	reward / (base_time_ms + probe_time_ms)	Reward per millisecond, including probe overhead	
utility_gain_per_probe_episode	utility_improvement / probe_episodes	Return on probing investment	
Usage Example
Use this Key-Door example to check how the tracker reports invocations and their binary rewards. It runs two task invocations for accounting. To measure a contribution or utility improvement, supply a runner, intervention and comparison under the protocol above.
from time import perf_counter

from reckon import CausalMemoryManager, MemoryBudget
from reckon.metrics import ProbeCostTracker, EfficiencyMetrics
from reckon.tasks.task_a_keydoor import KeyDoorTask

task = KeyDoorTask()
tracker = ProbeCostTracker()
base_episodes = 100
started = perf_counter()
baseline = task.run(
    CausalMemoryManager(MemoryBudget(max_slots=100, max_bytes=50_000)),
    num_episodes=base_episodes,
    seed=41,
)
tracker.set_base_costs(
    episodes=base_episodes,
    wall_time_ms=(perf_counter() - started) * 1000,
)

# Account for a second task run; no record-removal runner is invoked here.
with tracker.track_probe(probe_type="accounting-demo", seed=42):
    tracker.record_call(episodes=10)
    result = task.run(
        CausalMemoryManager(MemoryBudget(max_slots=100, max_bytes=50_000)),
        num_episodes=10,
        seed=42,
    )

summary = tracker.summarize()
print(f"Probe overhead: {summary.probe_overhead_ratio:.1%}")

# Key-Door awards one for a successful episode and zero otherwise.
total_reward = sum(
    episode["success"]
    for run in (baseline, result)
    for episode in run.raw_data["episodes"]
)
efficiency = EfficiencyMetrics.compute(
    total_reward=total_reward,
    probe_costs=summary,
)
print(f"Reward per total episode: {efficiency.reward_per_total_episode:.3f}")

Proto Schema
Probe costs are defined in protos/reckon/events.proto:
ProbeCostEvent: Per-probe operation costs
ProbeCostSummary: Aggregated probe metrics
Choose what a frontier compares
A frontier compares declared costs and outcomes. Choose the outcome explicitly and keep its producer, units and direction with the comparison. The dictionary and notebook helpers retain the axis names and reject missing or nonfinite measurements. An observed zero stays zero; an absent accuracy value cannot become success rate or a measured zero. This prevents an incomplete row from appearing artificially cheap or successful.
The notebook efficiency helper also requires a named outcome. Its overhead-weighted value is that outcome multiplied by one minus the fraction of episodes spent probing. That arithmetic does not establish a causal effect or decide whether the measurement cost is worthwhile.
For helper inputs, serialization and integration with tasks, use the metrics reference. The future service that returns signed evaluation artifacts has a separate planned contract.

body:
Continual retention confirmation
This protocol fixes the confirmation after the paired-input calibration (notebooks/runs/2026-11-16/continual_paired_calibration/53df3560dc14/summary.md). That calibration found small positive, negative and zero differences from learned utility, and a higher mean for no memory than for every retained-memory arm. Preserve those findings. The question is whether the implemented measured policy improves this workload relative to learned utility and to using no memory, at its full measurement price. It does not select a policy for adoption.
Fixed workload and sample
The configuration keeps three tasks, 40 training samples and 20 test samples per task, two features, replay probability 0.2 and learning rate 0.1. Each seed runs three episodes with carried memory and utility learning. Data and replay opportunities remain paired through the repaired streams. Use all 64 fresh outer seeds 50,000–50,063 exactly, with 49,999 reserved for the runner check and excluded from the confirmation. Do not change the task, policies or sample after observing outcomes.
Run no memory and full capacity once per seed, and FIFO, LRU, seeded random, explicit importance, learned utility, Diversity and measured retention at one and two slots, without a byte cap. This gives 16 rows, 1,024 seed runs and 3,072 main episodes. One slot is a structural control: admission has only one retained candidate to remove, so there is no ranking choice to compare. The two primary contrasts are measured minus learned utility at two slots, and measured at two slots minus no memory. All other comparisons are descriptive; full capacity is a reference with cost, not an accuracy upper bound.
Measured policy and probe price
At every measured pruning decision, test each current record in 64 fixed paired trials, using one fresh Continual episode in each arm. Both arms copy current memory; only the intervention removes the named record. Both use non-probing FIFO, carried memory and utility learning. The retained example can be read from the beginning of the episode. This remains a fresh-task comparison, not continuation of the live classifier. The equal-weight mixture of utility and positive intervention delta per byte is unchanged, and significance does not gate that ranking. Save every signed estimate and both outcomes.
Use paired t tests and Bonferroni correction across the candidates at each pruning decision, at family alpha 0.05. There are at most two candidates. Stored probe intervals remain individual 95% intervals, not family-adjusted intervals. Use no early stopping or adaptive sampling. The configuration retains the shared n_permutations field, but the selected t test does not use it. The larger fixed pair count and t test replace the calibration's four-pair diagnostic; the workload and retention formula remain unchanged.
For outer seed index i, start probe seeds at 4,000,000,000 + i * 100,000. Each decision advances by 64. At most 360 writes can occur in the three episodes, so at most 23,040 seed positions are needed per outer block. Both budgets share their assigned stream. The reserved runner check uses its separate diagnostic stream beginning at 2,000,000,000. Confirmation probe and main seeds are disjoint from the calibration and earlier experiments; smoke observations never enter inference.
Report main and probe episodes, writes, task and policy removals, sampled store peaks, actual initial-record reads, signed estimates, and inclusive and probe elapsed time. Inclusive time already includes measurement. Keep complete raw trials in compressed seed files; neither a low-cost empty probe nor a discarded adverse estimate may masquerade as the measured policy's result.
Planned inference
The unit is the outer seed's mean final accuracy over its three episodes. Use two-sided paired t tests for the two declared contrasts, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values and individual 97.5% intervals, giving family alpha 0.05. Report all 16 row means and sample standard deviations and retain both primary difference vectors. Equal observed values at one slot describe the control; no extra significance test is assigned to them.
The planning effect is 0.05 accuracy, five percentage points, with an assumed paired standard deviation of 0.10. This is an analyst-selected target, not Harsh's adoption threshold. At 64 independent pairs and per-comparison alpha 0.025, the noncentral-t calculation gives power 0.953329 under independent normal differences. The same conservative two-candidate calculation applies to the fixed 64-pair probes. The calibration's observed outer paired SD was 0.023384 and its largest four-pair probe SD was 0.055277; neither is a bound on future variance. Report actual spreads and intervals, and preserve this qualification if differences are discrete, non-normal or more variable than assumed. Do not replace planning power with a retrospective observed-effect calculation.
Compare intervals with both zero and the positive 0.05 target. Report a negative difference from no memory as prominently as a positive difference from utility. Failure to reject zero is not equivalence; a statistically detectable small gain is not evidence that its probe price is justified. The family adjustment covers these two outer contrasts and, separately, each probe decision's candidates, not every adaptively reached decision in the run. If all paired differences are equal, report zero sample variance and the degenerate interval explicitly.
Execution and interruption
Use python notebooks/experiments/workload_controls.py --config notebooks/experiments/continual_confirmation.json --plan to inspect the declaration and planning calculation without executing a task. Commit the protocol, configuration and runner before running the reserved --smoke OUTPUT_DIRECTORY, then --run. The runner records source, extension, lockfile and dependency identities, writes complete per-seed raw results and verifies that its inputs stayed unchanged before marking completion. It refuses to overwrite an existing run. Preserve any interrupted run as incomplete and reconcile its completed seeds before continuing; no optional stopping, replacement outcomes or added seeds are permitted.

body:
Tutor memory comparison
This protocol fixes the next Tutor comparison before its new seed outcomes are inspected. It follows the paired-input calibration (notebooks/runs/2026-11-15/tutor_paired_calibration/d1946209a918/summary.md), including its null and adverse findings. It tests the implemented retention policies on that one declared workload. The other native tasks and notebook adapters remain separate work; this result cannot establish the whole Reckon hypothesis.
Question and fixed inputs
Does measured retention improve the mean fraction of misconceptions cleared over learned utility at two or four memory slots, and what does its measurement cost? The configuration retains six initially misunderstood concepts, six questions in one session, a 0.3 base hint success probability and a 0.2 remembered-hint boost. Each seed runs five episodes with carried memory and utility learning. Starting students and response randomness are paired independently of action choices.
Compare no memory, full capacity, FIFO, LRU, seeded random, explicit importance, learned utility, Diversity and measured retention. Run the first two controls once per seed; run each limited policy at two and four slots. This gives 16 rows, each with 256 independent outer seeds and 1,280 main episodes: 20,480 main episodes altogether. Use seeds 20,000–20,255 exactly. Seeds 100–104 supplied exploratory findings; seed 105 is reserved for a runner check and excluded from inference. Do not change the workload or sample count after seeing confirmation outcomes.
A Beta-posterior arm is omitted from this experiment. The endpoint is an episode's fraction cleared, and no additional posterior-based retention rule has been specified and implemented for it. Relabelling the existing measured or utility policy would add no distinct comparator.
Probe declaration and price
At every measured-policy prune, test each retained record using 256 fixed paired trials, with one fresh Tutor episode in each arm. Copy the current memory into each trial, remove the named record only in the intervention arm, and use non-probing FIFO with utility learning inside both arms. This is a fresh-task experiment, not continuation of the live student's state. Keep the existing equal-weight mixture of utility and positive measured effect per byte; signed estimates remain in the raw evidence. Significance does not gate the ranking.
Use a paired t test and Bonferroni correction of its p-values over the candidates at that one pruning decision, at family alpha 0.05. The stored probe intervals remain individual 95% t intervals; they are not adjusted for the candidate family. There are at most four retained candidates under these budgets. Sampling has no early stopping. The t test replaces the four-pair exploratory permutation test so this declared larger comparison can retain a useful inferential resolution without spending most of its time on permutation draws. Its interval and power assumptions remain explicit. The n_permutations field is retained by the common configuration but unused by the selected t test.
For outer seed index i, start probe seeds at 10,000,000 + i * 1,000,000; each subsequent pruning decision advances by 256. Candidate records and the two budgets share the same index-specific probe stream, but outer seeds use disjoint streams. At most 30 writes can occur in five six-question episodes, so the reservation cannot overlap the next outer seed. Probe seeds are disjoint from all main seeds.
Retain every raw paired outcome, record snapshot, selected removal and cost in compressed per-seed result files. Report main and probe episodes, task and probe elapsed time, peak memory, writes and prunes separately. Total elapsed time includes measurement; it must not be presented as ordinary task time. Timing is an observation of this machine and run, not a universal performance claim.
Analysis fixed before the run
The two primary contrasts are measured minus learned utility at two slots and at four slots. The unit is the outer seed's mean across its five carried episodes, not each episode or probe. Use two-sided paired t tests with Bonferroni-adjusted p-values and 97.5% intervals for each contrast, giving a family alpha of 0.05. Report all 16 policy means with sample spreads and descriptive 95% t intervals; those individual intervals do not supply simultaneous policy rankings. Retain the two primary raw paired vectors.
A difference of 0.05 in the fraction cleared is an analyst-selected planning target: five percentage points. It is not Harsh's accepted threshold for a useful product or permission to promote a policy. With 256 outer seeds, a paired standard deviation of 0.25 and per-contrast alpha 0.025, the noncentral-t planning calculation gives power 0.8271 for a true difference of that size. With 256 probe pairs, paired standard deviation 0.20 and per-record alpha 0.0125 for four candidates, the corresponding planning power is 0.9303. These calculations assume independent normally distributed paired differences. Bounded, discrete simulation outcomes may depart from that approximation; larger variance reduces power. State observed spreads and interval widths alongside these assumptions, and do not substitute retrospective observed-effect power.
The probe planning power refers to rejection at the corrected per-record threshold, not coverage of the stored pointwise intervals. The runner calculates those figures using SciPy's noncentral t distribution; the final contrast uses the paired t test. The run does not claim simultaneous error control over every adaptively reached pruning decision. Per-decision probe inference and the fixed outer policy comparison answer different questions.
Report negative and null differences with the same prominence as positive ones. Failure to reject zero does not establish equivalence. A positive estimate alone does not establish a benefit of at least 0.05: compare the interval with both zero and the planning target. Even an interval wholly above the target leaves the measured policy's compute price and the workload's scope to assess.
Execution and interruption
Review and commit this protocol, configuration and runner before starting the confirmation seeds. The runner records source and environment identities, copies its exact inputs, and writes each completed seed atomically. Resume only when those identities and the saved file hashes still match. Interruption may leave a partial run, which must remain labelled incomplete; it cannot supply the planned final test. Do not replace completed observations or add seeds to obtain a preferred result.
Run python notebooks/experiments/tutor_confirmation.py --plan to inspect the settings and planning calculation without executing a task. The --smoke OUTPUT_DIRECTORY route runs only reserved seed 105 and checks result structure and accounting. Run --run after review to execute or resume the fixed confirmation. A source or configuration repair after confirmation starts needs a separately identified protocol and run; preserve the affected results and state the reason.

The stored probe intervals remain individual 95% t intervals; they are not adjusted for the candidate family. There are at most four retained candidates under these budgets. Sampling has no early stopping. The t test replaces the four-pair exploratory permutation test so this declared larger comparison can retain a useful inferential resolution without spending most of its time on permutation draws. Its interval and power assumptions remain explicit. The n_permutations field is retained by the common configuration but unused by the selected t test.
For outer seed index i, start probe seeds at 10,000,000 + i * 1,000,000; each subsequent pruning decision advances by 256. Candidate records and the two budgets share the same index-specific probe stream, but outer seeds use disjoint streams. At most 30 writes can occur in five six-question episodes, so the reservation cannot overlap the next outer seed. Probe seeds are disjoint from all main seeds.
Retain every raw paired outcome, record snapshot, selected removal and cost in compressed per-seed result files. Report main and probe episodes, task and probe elapsed time, peak memory, writes and prunes separately. Total elapsed time includes measurement; it must not be presented as ordinary task time. Timing is an observation of this machine and run, not a universal performance claim.
Analysis fixed before the run
The two primary contrasts are measured minus learned utility at two slots and at four slots. The unit is the outer seed's mean across its five carried episodes, not each episode or probe. Use two-sided paired t tests with Bonferroni-adjusted p-values and 97.5% intervals for each contrast, giving a family alpha of 0.05. Report all 16 policy means with sample spreads and descriptive 95% t intervals; those individual intervals do not supply simultaneous policy rankings. Retain the two primary raw paired vectors.
A difference of 0.05 in the fraction cleared is an analyst-selected planning target: five percentage points. It is not Harsh's accepted threshold for a useful product or permission to promote a policy. With 256 outer seeds, a paired standard deviation of 0.25 and per-contrast alpha 0.025, the noncentral-t planning calculation gives power 0.8271 for a true difference of that size. With 256 probe pairs, paired standard deviation 0.20 and per-record alpha 0.0125 for four candidates, the corresponding planning power is 0.9303. These calculations assume independent normally distributed paired differences. Bounded, discrete simulation outcomes may depart from that approximation; larger variance reduces power. State observed spreads and interval widths alongside these assumptions, and do not substitute retrospective observed-effect power.
The probe planning power refers to rejection at the corrected per-record threshold, not coverage of the stored pointwise intervals. The runner calculates those figures using SciPy's noncentral t distribution; the final contrast uses the paired t test. The run does not claim simultaneous error control over every adaptively reached pruning decision. Per-decision probe inference and the fixed outer policy comparison answer different questions.
Report negative and null differences with the same prominence as positive ones. Failure to reject zero does not establish equivalence. A positive estimate alone does not establish a benefit of at least 0.05: compare the interval with both zero and the planning target. Even an interval wholly above the target leaves the measured policy's compute price and the workload's scope to assess.
Execution and interruption
Review and commit this protocol, configuration and runner before starting the confirmation seeds. The runner records source and environment identities, copies its exact inputs, and writes each completed seed atomically. Resume only when those identities and the saved file hashes still match. Interruption may leave a partial run, which must remain labelled incomplete; it cannot supply the planned final test. Do not replace completed observations or add seeds to obtain a preferred result.
Run python notebooks/experiments/tutor_confirmation.py --plan to inspect the settings and planning calculation without executing a task. The --smoke OUTPUT_DIRECTORY route runs only reserved seed 105 and checks result structure and accounting. Run --run after review to execute or resume the fixed confirmation. A source or configuration repair after confirmation starts needs a separately identified protocol and run; preserve the affected results and state the reason.

body:
Frequently Asked Questions
Use these answers when choosing a policy, connecting a task or diagnosing a run. For a first experiment, start with Compare two replay budgets.
Framework Questions
Q: Does the laboratory require quantum mechanics?
No. The framework is stated generally (arrow-neutral dynamics), but all benchmarks and implementations use classical systems. Quantum references are for theoretical completeness and future extensions.
Q: Is this just another replay buffer?
A replay buffer is one use of the memory manager. The same record API can hold cues, observations or reasoning traces, with a chosen retention policy and saved operation logs. The laboratory adds tasks and analysis tools for comparing those choices. Start with the replay-budget comparison for a complete learner example; it compares memory allowances, not causal effects of individual records.
Q: Why "arrow-neutral"?
The framework starts with dynamics that do not assume a preferred direction of time. Thermodynamic arrows need a coarse-graining and boundary conditions. This keeps those assumptions explicit instead of building them into the microscopic law.
Implementation Questions
Q: What if I don't know the causal scores?
You can store and retrieve records without them. Use FIFO, LRU or a utility-based policy for the comparison you want to run. A supplied prediction-error score can guide retention, but it remains a heuristic. For a removal test, use a runner that removes the record at the point where the task would use it. Check the current evaluator’s limits in the evaluation protocol.
Q: Can I use this with LLMs?
The manager can store records for a custom agent loop, but it does not automatically manage a model's context window. Your adapter must decide what to write, how to retrieve it, how to assemble the prompt and which outcome updates utility. The conversation notebook can use a simulated backend or a local Ollama model. See the notebook guide for the switch. The software is for local research and has no public release or supported model integration.
Q: How do I integrate with my RL framework?
Start with Connect retrieval to an outcome. Your task supplies observations, actions and rewards; the manager supplies write, retrieval and retention. Keep retrievals for one decision in an EpisodeContext before assigning its outcome. set_episode() resets stores and the logger by default; reset_memory=False carries records, scores and retained events. Save needed events before a reset or before the finite buffer overwrites them. The memory reference covers the API and current budget limits.
Debugging Questions
Q: The agent failed. How do I know if it's a memory problem?
Use the timeline view of the debugger to inspect writes, reads and prunes around the failure, matching their record IDs to the cue records retained by your experiment. Minimal operation logs do not preserve full payloads or tags, so a timeline alone may not identify the cue. For an older causal_precision value, first identify its producer and source revision: those keys carried different usage and outcome summaries. Current task results name their diagnostics explicitly, including one_minus_mean_forgetting and the distinct episode and pooled hint-read fractions. The current record evaluator separately counts beneficial significant interventions. None alone diagnoses the cause of a failed task. The metrics reference explains those meanings and the intervention evidence needed for a causal interpretation.
Q: What's "representation drift"?
When the agent's internal embeddings change over time in ways that break previously learned associations. The debugger design describes optional spectral tracking for this question. The current debugger application exposes Timeline, Relationship graph and Pareto Frontier views; it does not implement that drift panel.
Implementation References
Memory Module README: CMM API (write, read, prune, update_score)
Debugger Server README: FastAPI backend
Debugger UI README: React visualization components

body:
Framework overview

Reckon uses a research model to ask which observations an agent can keep and test under resource limits. Start here to see how those questions relate to the memory manager, evaluation code and debugger.
Layers
The model distinguishes the underlying dynamics, the observations an agent can make and the conclusions it can draw from them.
Layer 1: Microdynamics (arrow-neutral)
Assume closed evolution is reversible and measure-preserving (classical) or unitary (quantum). Fine-grained entropy is invariant here. No arrow is assumed in the micro-law.
Layer 2: Observer interface (where arrows enter)
For scale s and resources R, the interface has three parts. The coarse-graining Π_s determines what the agent observes. The record channel C_R determines what it can store and read back under noise. The allowed operations Op_R determine what it can change in an experiment.
Thermodynamic arrows arise only after:
choosing Π_s and resolution,
adding boundary conditions (e.g., Past Hypothesis),
invoking typicality arguments.
Layer 3: Operational causality and retrodiction
Use operational causality to ask whether an intervention changes what can be reliably observed under R. The resulting relation can fail reflexivity and transitivity. Use retrodiction to ask whether you can recover an earlier state from later records, given what the observation map preserves, how inverse errors grow and how noisy the records are.
The engineering translation
The memory manager stores typed records and decides when to remove them. Evaluation helpers summarize outcomes and test supplied comparisons. The debugger shows activity from a run you saved.
Note

Abstract interfaces do not establish the model. The channel interfaces are abstract classes, not concrete implementations of mathematical coarse-graining or reliable recording. The memory manager explains current budget enforcement and retrieval. The evaluation protocol describes the intervention-timing limits; the debugger guide distinguishes recorded operations from snapshots and measured contribution evidence.
Implementation
Component	Design Doc	Implementation	
Core abstractions	03-Math-Core.md	core/README.md	
Causal Memory Manager	08-Causal-Memory-Manager-Design.md	memory/README.md	
Debugger	10-Debugger-Visualization.md	viz/README.md, viz-ui/README.md	
Performance layer	none	kernel/README.md

body:
Glossary
Look up the terms used in the memory API, the mathematical chapters and task results. For a field from a saved run, start with the metric’s producer to find how it was computed.
Core Terms
Arrow-neutral: The microscopic law assumes no preferred direction of time. In MONAD’s model, the fine-grained entropy is invariant under the chosen evolution and so supplies no direction.
Causal Memory Manager (CMM): The core component of the laboratory that manages record storage, retention, and retrieval under resource budgets.
Resource-indexed influence (\preceq_R): A resource-indexed relation where A \preceq_R B means varying A produces detectable changes in reliable records of B under allowed protocols. It is neither reflexive nor transitive in general; DirectInfluenceRecords stores observations of its pairs.
Distinguishability threshold (\eta): The minimum divergence required to declare A \preceq_R B. Resolving a smaller effect may require more observations; the cost depends on the experiment, noise model and required error rates. Changing a stored threshold alone does not carry out that measurement.
Divergence D(\cdot \| \cdot): A measure of distinguishability between distributions. Allowed choices include KL divergence, total variation, and Hellinger distance. See Math-Core Section 5.
Coarse-graining (\Pi_s): A map from microstates to macrostates at scale s, determining which distinctions are observed. MONAD’s formal profile uses a deterministic measurable map, followed by a separate noisy record channel; the abstract laboratory interface does not supply a stochastic generalization.
Fine-grained entropy: Entropy of the full microstate distribution. It is invariant under invertible evolution that preserves the reference measure.
Macro-entropy: Entropy computed relative to a chosen coarse-graining; can increase even when fine-grained entropy is constant.
MemoryRecord: A typed object storing payload, cost, tags, creation metadata and utility estimates.
Operational causality: Causality defined by what an agent can reliably record and influence under its resource constraints.
Mutual influence: A and B influence each other when A \preceq_R B and B \preceq_R A. It is a symmetric relation, not an equivalence, because influence is neither reflexive nor transitive in general.
Allowed interventions (\text{Op}_R): The set of physically implementable preparations/controls under resource constraints R. See Operational Causality.
Protocol class: The set of allowed experimental procedures (preparation, evolution, coarse-graining, recording) under given resources.
Record channel (\mathcal{C}_R): A noisy storage/measurement channel mapping observations to stored records under resources R.
Resource vector (R): The multi-dimensional budget an agent operates under: memory slots, tokens, bytes, bandwidth, compute, noise floor.
Retrodiction: Inferring a past state or property from current records. The answer depends on what the observations can distinguish, how errors grow and how noisy the records are.
Reliable record: A record that lets you distinguish alternatives within the allowed trials and error rates. A record can persist without passing that test.
Benchmark Terms
Causal precision: A proposed evaluation target: the fraction of stored records meeting the declared positive-usefulness intervention test. The working evaluator instead reports contract_precision over distinct evaluated target labels, counting only beneficial significant effects. Its two-sided is_significant flag also admits harmful effects, so it is not the usefulness numerator. See Evaluation Metrics.
Causal recall: The target fraction of ground-truth necessary records retained. The record-summary helper names this supplied-label calculation necessary_cue_retention. The evaluator's contract_recall asks a different question: what fraction of supplied ground-truth target labels had beneficial significant effects? Its recall is unavailable without a non-empty label set. Evaluation Metrics defines both denominators.
Useful memory rate: The proposed fraction of stored items retrieved and shown to affect a decision. Current activity ratios have narrower names: useful_reads_per_read uses supplied useful reads, and Key-Door's successful_key_episodes_per_write uses useful writes. Neither denominator is distinct stored items, and neither calculation performs an ablation. See Evaluation Metrics.
Note

Read historical fields through their producer. Earlier saved results used these broad names for several different quantities. Interpret them through their captured producer and source revision; they are not aliases for the current fields.
Implementation References
For code implementations of these concepts, see:
Core Module README: ResourceVector, MemoryBudget, CoarseGraining, RecordChannel, DirectInfluenceRecords
Memory Module README: CausalMemoryManager, MemoryRecord, retention policies
Metrics Module README: task outcomes, memory activity, record summaries and intervention results

body:
Installation and a first run
Build a wheel for your Python interpreter, then import the Rust extension and run a task to check the build. The library and daemon build from this checkout without a sibling repository.
Before you begin
Install these tools before building:
Tool	Requirement	
Shell	Bash for the activation commands	
Python	CPython 3.9–3.12 with virtual-environment support; this guide uses 3.11	
Rust and Cargo	Use a toolchain supported by the resolved dependencies. The kernel declares Rust 1.75; the dependency versions you build can require a newer release.	
System tools	A linker; Cargo supplies the Protocol Buffers compiler	
Git	Access to the Reckon source repository	
Use CPython 3.11 for the steps below. The extension builds with PyO3 0.20.3 and targets the abi3-py39 ABI. The package metadata allows >=3.9. If you use a Python version outside the documented range, run the import check on your machine before starting an experiment.
The optional Python wire messages and gRPC client require Python 3.10+ through the rpc extra; generation uses proto. Python 3.9 remains supported for the core library. See the wire guide for installation and calls.
When repeating an experiment, check out the Reckon revision and dependency lockfiles recorded with that run. Older revisions that declared a MONAD dependency still need the matching MONAD source captured with their evidence.
The Rust builds use the pinned compiler unless PROTOC selects another executable. A separately installed protoc is optional. Offline builds need the packaged compiler dependencies in Cargo's cache along with the other dependencies.
Set up the environment
Check out Reckon
Clone the selected source:
git clone https://github.com/getHarshOnline/reckon.git
cd reckon

Create the Python environment
Use an installed CPython 3.11 explicitly. Choose an unused environment directory; if .venv-311 already exists, choose another name rather than replacing it.
python3.11 -m venv .venv-311
source .venv-311/bin/activate
python --version
python -m pip install "maturin>=1.4,<2.0"

Check that the reported version is 3.11. Activating an existing environment does not change the interpreter that created it.
Build and install the package
From the Reckon repository root, build a wheel with that interpreter:
maturin build --interpreter "$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/python" --out "$VIRTUAL_ENV/wheels"
python -m pip install "$VIRTUAL_ENV"/wheels/*.whl

The wheel and its base dependencies supply the Python package, NumPy and SciPy. Install optional debugger, test or notebook dependencies for the workflow that needs them. To build with a recorded kernel/Cargo.lock, supply that lockfile and add --locked. See what to capture for a repeatable build.
Verify the extension
python -c "from reckon._rust import EventLogger, RecordStore"

The command exits silently when Python can load the compiled extension. If it fails, check that the active interpreter matches the wheel and follow the kernel build procedure. The package requires the extension.
Keep this environment active for the commands below. Install the notebook runner, table and plotting packages with python -m pip install ".[notebooks]". The notebook guide covers optional environment integrations.
The optional setup.sh helper uses the repository’s .venv and installs the dev,viz extras. If the directory is missing, the script creates it using the python3 on your path. Create an unused environment with a supported interpreter first or check the interpreter in an existing .venv. Use a fresh directory if you need to switch interpreters.
Warning

Verify the extension import. The helper can finish after a failed extension build, so verify the import before using the environment.
If you came from Compare replay budgets, return there with this environment active. For Inspect an exported run, add the Python visualization dependencies with python -m pip install ".[viz]", then install Node.js 18 or later and pnpm 9 for the interface. Neither task needs the daemon.
Check that it works
List the available tasks, then run ten Key-Door episodes:
reckon list
reckon run --task keydoor --episodes 10

Look for a task result after reckon list reports the available runners. The command checks that the task and extension can run together. For changes to the implementation, run its tests.
Use the memory manager
Use the following to check the Python integration after the build. It stores an observation, retrieves it by tag and updates the stored record’s utility.
from reckon import CausalMemoryManager, MemoryBudget, PayloadType

memory = CausalMemoryManager(MemoryBudget(max_slots=100, max_bytes=50_000))
record_id = memory.write(
    payload={"observation": "key is in room A"},
    payload_type=PayloadType.OBSERVATION,
    tags=["key", "location"],
)
hits = memory.retrieve(query={"tags": ["key"]})
memory.update_score(record_id, "utility", value=10.0, signal_source="reward")

For a complete integration with expected output, connect retrieval to an outcome. The memory manager chapter explains retention and how the selected policy enforces byte, slot and declared-token limits together.
Open the debugger
For the startup and import walkthrough, follow Inspect an exported run. To produce debugger-compatible data or embed a view, use the debugger data contract and server API.
The daemon is for your own machine only
The gRPC daemon keeps its own in-memory store. It defaults to 127.0.0.1, rejects non-loopback addresses and uses plaintext without caller authentication:
(cd daemon && cargo run --release -- --host 127.0.0.1)

Warning

Use it only on a trusted local machine. It is separate from the Python manager and debugger. Its record-only ExportRun selects records written or retrieved by a named run; event, metric and archive attachments remain unimplemented. It does not yet produce a complete debugger run bundle.

The command exits silently when Python can load the compiled extension. If it fails, check that the active interpreter matches the wheel and follow the kernel build procedure. The package requires the extension.
Keep this environment active for the commands below. Install the notebook runner, table and plotting packages with python -m pip install ".[notebooks]". The notebook guide covers optional environment integrations.
The optional setup.sh helper uses the repository’s .venv and installs the dev,viz extras. If the directory is missing, the script creates it using the python3 on your path. Create an unused environment with a supported interpreter first or check the interpreter in an existing .venv. Use a fresh directory if you need to switch interpreters.
Warning

Verify the extension import. The helper can finish after a failed extension build, so verify the import before using the environment.
If you came from Compare replay budgets, return there with this environment active. For Inspect an exported run, add the Python visualization dependencies with python -m pip install ".[viz]", then install Node.js 18 or later and pnpm 9 for the interface. Neither task needs the daemon.
Check that it works
List the available tasks, then run ten Key-Door episodes:
reckon list
reckon run --task keydoor --episodes 10

Look for a task result after reckon list reports the available runners. The command checks that the task and extension can run together. For changes to the implementation, run its tests.
Use the memory manager
Use the following to check the Python integration after the build. It stores an observation, retrieves it by tag and updates the stored record’s utility.
from reckon import CausalMemoryManager, MemoryBudget, PayloadType

memory = CausalMemoryManager(MemoryBudget(max_slots=100, max_bytes=50_000))
record_id = memory.write(
    payload={"observation": "key is in room A"},
    payload_type=PayloadType.OBSERVATION,
    tags=["key", "location"],
)
hits = memory.retrieve(query={"tags": ["key"]})
memory.update_score(record_id, "utility", value=10.0, signal_source="reward")

For a complete integration with expected output, connect retrieval to an outcome. The memory manager chapter explains retention and how the selected policy enforces byte, slot and declared-token limits together.
Open the debugger
For the startup and import walkthrough, follow Inspect an exported run. To produce debugger-compatible data or embed a view, use the debugger data contract and server API.
The daemon is for your own machine only
The gRPC daemon keeps its own in-memory store. It defaults to 127.0.0.1, rejects non-loopback addresses and uses plaintext without caller authentication:
(cd daemon && cargo run --release -- --host 127.0.0.1)

Warning

Use it only on a trusted local machine. It is separate from the Python manager and debugger. Its record-only ExportRun selects records written or retrieved by a named run; event, metric and archive attachments remain unimplemented. It does not yet produce a complete debugger run bundle.

Reckon Rust Core
The Rust kernel of Reckon's laboratory: its record store, credit updates and event log.
Purpose
This crate provides the performance-critical components of Reckon. Rust consumers build it without Python by default. The python feature enables its PyO3 bindings, and extension-module also selects the linking mode used by the Python package. Maturin selects that feature through the root pyproject.toml. Python accesses the kernel through reckon._rust; the extension remains required and there is no pure Python fallback.
Components
Credit and utility (credit.rs)
Python and the gRPC daemon call one implementation of equal, shaped and ablation-based credit, followed by the bounded moving-average update. SHAPED uses stable softplus at an explicit positive scale; the laboratory default is 1.0. ABLATION normalizes positive measured deltas, returns zero weights when measurements exist but none is positive, and uses equal credit only when all measurements are absent. Neither call changes the stored measurements. Invalid input fails before callers apply the observation's updates. See the Python core guide for defaults and input domains.
RecordStore (store.rs)
Thread-safe record storage with priority indexing.
The kernel index and daemon capacity pruning share retention_priority: utility plus half the positive parts of the ablation and counterfactual measurements. Missing or NaN measurements add no bonus; a NaN total sorts first for removal. Both break equal scores by record ID. Proxy magnitude and cost do not enter this store ranking.
Component	Data Structure	Purpose	
records	hashbrown::HashMap	O(1) record lookup	
priority_index	BinaryHeap	O(log n) pruning selection	
current_bytes, current_tokens	parking_lot::RwLock<i64>	Track declared byte and token totals	
Key operations:
insert(): Add record, update index
get(): O(1) lookup by ID
remove(): Delete record, update usage
select_for_pruning(): Return lowest-priority records
touch(): Update access stats
fork(): Copy complete records, priorities and accounting for an independent in-memory trial
fork() holds the record lock while copying the other store components in their declared lock order. The copy keeps the slot capacity and every native admission field. Its Python binding also deep-copies the live record objects, preserving shared references within the copy and separating mutations from the original. The manager starts a fresh trial log and operation windows. This is an in-memory operation, not persistence or a replay format.
insert() returns Result<Option<Record>, RecordStoreError>. A successful replacement returns the old record; a new ID returns None inside Ok. Negative byte or token costs and either total above the signed 64-bit range are refused before records, priorities or accounting change. The final-total check deducts a replacement's old cost and runs under the store's mutation lock. Native zero-byte records remain valid. The caller enforces its byte, slot and token budgets and chooses any removals; capacity() reports the declared slot capacity.
touch() returns Result<bool, RecordStoreError>: Ok(true) when updated and Ok(false) for a missing ID. At the signed 32-bit access-count maximum, it returns UseCountOverflow before changing either the count or last-access timestamp. Python receives OverflowError; ordinary calls still return a Boolean.
Complete laboratory records
record.rs owns the laboratory record, cost, origin, utility, score and payload-kind model. The PyO3 adapters use the same generic record structure with Python references for opaque payloads and mutable containers. The manager calls prepare_object() before choosing budget removals, then retains the native object and its validated admission projection with insert_object(). That projection retains the original costs even when a caller edits returned metadata. The Python facade preserves dataclass helpers, copying, pickling and cyclic references, and the bindings participate in Python garbage collection.
The default exchange representation carries explicitly encoded payload and metadata bytes. MemoryRecord.snapshot_json(payload_bytes, metadata_bytes) leaves the live objects intact, represents int64 fields as decimal strings and keeps unknown tokens as null. Byte/step/token values use signed 64-bit storage; slot/access counts use signed 32-bit storage. JSON export refuses non-finite utility or score values. snapshot_wire() uses the historical laboratory protobuf format and refuses an unknown token count, since its scalar field cannot express one.
Record::try_from(proto::MemoryRecord) and the reverse conversion preserve every declared laboratory field through storage, copying and removal: opaque payload and metadata bytes, compression labels, ordered tags, supplied origin, utility and score fields, and optional creation positions. The conversion requires cost, utility and causal-score messages and refuses unknown payload kinds. It preserves absent origin and optional measurements, including the difference between absent and measured zero. Signed 64-bit values remain exact. The laboratory schema's token count is a scalar, so its wire value does not distinguish unknown from zero.
Low-level callers can still use Record.from_wire(data), store.insert_record(record) and record.to_wire() with generated historical laboratory messages. This byte route does not serialize arbitrary Python objects. Both insert() and insert_record() refuse an ID already backed by a live object with ValueError, before changing either view or its accounting. Remove that entry explicitly before changing its representation. The scalar token value always remains numeric, including zero. The daemon's core.v1.Record, with typed tags and links, remains a separate contract. Protobuf unknown fields are not retained by the native decoder.
From viz-ui/, run pnpm generate:records to emit the Rust-derived TypeScript and JSON Schema; component builds run this step automatically. The outputs under packages/components/src/generated/ and kernel/generated/ are excluded build artifacts. node scripts/generate-records.mjs --check compares them with the current model. Python can obtain the same schema from reckon._rust.record_schema(). The descriptions do not replace validation: the browser adapter refuses int64 values outside JavaScript's exact integer range.
PriorityIndex
The heap uses lazy deletion. insert(id, priority) pushes a RecordRef. update(id, new_priority) marks the previous entry invalid and pushes the new one. pop_lowest() skips invalid entries. Call rebuild() to reconstruct the heap.
EventLogger (logging.rs)
High-frequency event ring buffer:
Component	Purpose	
buffer	VecDeque with fixed capacity	
counter	Atomic event ID generator	
episode_id	Current episode context	
Operations:
log() / log_full(): Add event to buffer
drain(): Return and clear all events
since(event_id): Get events after ID
to_jsonl(): Export as JSON Lines
Retention Policies (policies.rs)
The Rust policy trait and Python laboratory wrappers call select_retention, which returns the shortest ranked prefix meeting byte, record-slot and token pressure. The Rust trait returns a Result; invalid costs, repeated IDs, non-finite selected scores and invalid weights are errors. A request exceeding the whole input returns every record, leaving its caller to refuse infeasible admission before mutation. Equal ranking keys preserve input order. Token costs use the existing Record.cost_tokens field and a separate stopping threshold; token pressure does not alter the ranking or its byte denominator. select_retention and select_for_budget take token pressure after slot pressure, and the byte-only select_for_pruning trait method supplies zero for the other dimensions.
Policy	Selection Criterion	
FifoPolicy	Oldest first (by timestamp)	
LruPolicy	Least recently used	
UtilityPolicy	Lowest raw utility first	
WeightedEvidencePolicy	Lowest weighted combination of utility, measured effects and proxy magnitude	
DiversityPolicy	Lowest raw utility in a round-robin traversal of payload types

Python's EvidencePerBytePolicy chooses EvidencePerByte; Rust's WeightedEvidencePolicy chooses WeightedEvidence. See the policy distinction before comparing results. Python's importance arm supplies its declared importance as the per-byte score, and its random arm supplies the existing seeded order; both use the same prefix-selection rule.

Its name is WeightedEvidence and its log reason is weighted_evidence_lowest. Earlier saved records retain their original policy name and source revision.
Diversity groups payload types in lexical order, removes their low-utility surplus round-robin, then continues below the requested per-type minimum when capacity requires it. The minimum is a preference, not a guarantee that can defeat the budget. The Python comparison runner exposes this same rule as diversity.
Measured ablation and counterfactual deltas retain their signs in records. WeightedEvidencePolicy and the store’s priority index give a harmful effect zero retention bonus; utility remains separate. The policy’s proxy component keeps its magnitude-based meaning. This sign rule does not make the Python policy, Rust policy and store priority the same ranking; their separate formulas remain on the policy score page.
PyO3 Integration
Exposed Types
Rust Type	Python Name	Purpose	
PyRecordStore	RecordStore	Record storage	
PyRecord	Record	Single record	
PyEventLogger	EventLogger	Event logging	
PyRetentionPolicy	RetentionPolicy	Policy selection	
Python Usage
from reckon._rust import RecordStore, EventLogger

store = RecordStore(max_slots=10000)
logger = EventLogger(capacity=10000)

Type stubs in src/reckon/_rust.pyi provide IDE support.
Performance Characteristics
Target Metrics
Operation	Target	Mechanism	
write()	< 100us	Via HashMap insert + heap push	
read()	< 50us	Via HashMap lookup	
select_for_pruning(10K)	< 1ms	Via BinaryHeap	
The timings are design targets. The listed data structures explain the implementation; they do not establish measured latency or attainment of those targets.
Measure the native store
Run cargo bench --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml --bench store_bench -- --noplot from the repository root. The benchmark measures three batches: inserting 1,000 prepared 100-byte records, reading 100 evenly spaced keys from 1,000 records, and selecting 100 records from a 10,000-record store. Selection identifies records totaling 10,000 bytes and leaves them stored. The read keys are fixed, not random.
Fixture construction is outside the timed operations. Insertion also excludes destruction of the resulting store; reads include cloning and dropping each returned record, and selection includes restoring the index and dropping the returned IDs. Criterion uses 30 samples with a one-second warmup and three-second measurement window per case. Its estimates and raw samples go under kernel/target/criterion/. Batch timings and per-record throughput are different quantities; neither establishes the Python API's latency or a memory-policy benefit.
The 15 November 2026 measurement retains the raw samples, estimates, source hashes and toolchain. It predates the direct-insert cost and overflow checks. On an Apple M4 Max with macOS ARM64 and Rust 1.94.0, while other development work was active, the estimated batch times were:
Batch	Estimate	95% confidence interval	
Insert 1,000 records	433.52 µs	345.83–521.70 µs	
Read 100 keys	32.92 µs	28.38–39.07 µs	
Select 100 of 10,000 records	34.32 µs	28.31–41.82 µs	
These are observations from one shared development host and one workload, not a latency guarantee. Re-run the command on the intended deployment workload before comparing it with the targets above.
Memory Layout
Records stored by value in HashMap
PriorityIndex stores lightweight RecordRef (ID + priority)
Lazy deletion avoids heap rebuild on updates
Future storage and performance choices
The current kernel keeps records and events in memory. The following choices are conditional design work; the native store measurements provide a baseline for deciding what needs to change.
Batch statistics. Consider faer for the probe's numerical batches only when profiling a measured experiment identifies those calculations as a material cost. Measure that cost separately from running the paired task episodes, copying memory and collecting results. A faster calculation must preserve the experiment's estimates and uncertainty; the reproducibility guide defines the comparison it serves. faer is not a current dependency.
Graph dependencies. The kernel has no runtime use of petgraph and no MONAD source dependency. The resolved build still includes petgraph through prost-build, the protocol compiler listed in Cargo.toml. That build dependency supplies no graph capability to Reckon's record store. Add a runtime graph representation only for an identified operation and its data requirements.
Durable records and replay. A future laboratory store must define what survives a restart and retain enough record state and ordered operations to reconstruct the run it promises to replay. The current event ring can overwrite entries and omits full record state; RecordStore.fork() makes an independent in-memory trial. The debugger's RunStore saves supplied event files and summaries for viewing. Those exports remain useful, but recovering the live manager requires a separate persistence and replay contract, including how an interrupted write is handled.
Arena allocation. Consider a generational slot arena only if measurements of the intended workload identify the map and heap as the store's bottleneck. The existing batch timings alone do not establish that cause. Share reusable arena and ring mechanics through rtepl-common when that work is justified. Reckon keeps the meaning of its records, budgets and retention policies; Pale keeps the meaning of its own graph and scheduling state. Shared storage mechanics must preserve those separate contracts.
Linux I/O. Consider an io_uring adapter only after a durable store and a Linux deployment exist. The adapter owns its pinned I/O buffers; the record arena has a separate lifetime. Its portable fallback must produce identical stored and replayed results for the same operations. Establish the store's correctness and recovery behavior before comparing I/O throughput.
Building
Follow installation for a new CPython 3.11 environment. The documented CPython range is 3.9–3.12. Pass the interpreter explicitly so the build and import check use the same environment. Run the commands below from the Reckon repository root.
Protocol Buffers compiler
The kernel and daemon build scripts use protoc-bin-vendored = 3.3.0, which supplies protoc 36.2 for the build host. Cargo fetches those packages with the other build dependencies; installing a system compiler is optional. Rust consumers such as HENA and Q-HENA inherit this build requirement through the kernel. An offline build needs the packaged compiler in Cargo's cache.
Set PROTOC to an executable path to select a compiler explicitly. PROTOC_INCLUDE can select its include directory. When choosing the packaged compiler, the build also uses its packaged includes unless PROTOC_INCLUDE is already set. Cargo reruns generation when either selection changes. Generated Rust stays in Cargo's build output directory.
Development
(cd kernel && cargo build)

This builds the Rust API without PyO3. The daemon and Rust re-export consumers use that default. The kernel has no sibling source dependency. MONAD remains the manual’s source of formal definitions; no implemented kernel path uses its types. Use cargo check --features python in kernel/ when checking the binding without extension-module linking.
Run cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml --test store_properties for the exhaustive small-state checks. They compare 32,768 length-five operation traces with an independent map, checking replacement, removal, utility/access updates, pruning, rebuilding, accounting and repeatable priority selection. A second property checks all 341 cost vectors of up to four records over zero, small and large costs, across 13 policy configurations and feasible or infeasible byte/slot pressures. These tests cover valid input domains; RecordStore leaves admission limits to its caller.
Python Extension
# With the supported project environment active, from the repository root
maturin build --interpreter "$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/python" --out "$VIRTUAL_ENV/wheels"
python -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps "$VIRTUAL_ENV"/wheels/*.whl
python -c "from reckon._rust import EventLogger, RecordStore"

The installation guide installs the runtime dependencies before this rebuild. --force-reinstall --no-deps replaces the installed package with the new wheel while keeping those dependencies. cargo build alone does not refresh the Python extension. For editable Python development, maturin develop uses the active supported environment and writes its extension into the source package; do not use that route when preserving an existing source-tree extension.
Release
# From the repository root with the project environment active
maturin build --release --interpreter "$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/python"

Proto Integration
Types are generated from Protocol Buffers via prost:
// build.rs
prost_build::compile_protos(&["../protos/reckon/record.proto"], &["../protos"])?;

// lib.rs
pub mod proto {
    include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/reckon.rs"));
}

Lock Ordering
To prevent deadlocks in RecordStore, always acquire locks in this order:
records (RwLock)
priority_index (RwLock)
current_bytes (RwLock)
current_tokens (RwLock)
Never hold priority_index while acquiring records.
Error Handling
The crate uses thiserror for error definitions. Common error patterns:
Record not found: Returns Option<Record> (None if missing)
Insert with duplicate ID: Returns Ok(Some(record)) containing the replaced record
Negative byte or token cost, or either overflowing total: Returns RecordStoreError without mutation; Python receives ValueError or OverflowError, respectively
Buffer overflow: Events are dropped (check dropped_count())
Tracing Instrumentation
Key operations are instrumented with tracing:
use tracing::{instrument, debug};

#[instrument(skip(self))]
pub fn insert(&self, record: Record) -> Option<Record> {
    debug!(id = %record.id, "inserting record");
    // ...
}

Enable tracing by configuring a subscriber in your Python code or Rust tests.
Source map and dependencies
Architecture
flowchart TB
    subgraph Crate["reckon"]
        Lib["lib.rs\n(PyO3 module)"]
        Store["store.rs\n(RecordStore)"]
        Policies["policies.rs\n(RetentionPolicy)"]
        Logging["logging.rs\n(EventLogger)"]
        Proto["generated/\n(prost types)"]
    end

    subgraph Python["Python Layer"]
        CMM["CausalMemoryManager"]
        PyStore["_rust.RecordStore"]
        PyLogger["_rust.EventLogger"]
    end

    subgraph External["External"]
        Protos["protos/*.proto"]
        Build["build.rs"]
    end

    Lib --> Store
    Lib --> Policies
    Lib --> Logging
    Store --> Proto
    Build --> Protos
    Protos --> Proto

    CMM --> PyStore
    CMM --> PyLogger
    PyStore --> Store
    PyLogger --> Logging

Module Structure
Start in store.rs to trace a lookup or change index maintenance, logging.rs for buffer behavior, and policies.rs for the Rust-side rankings.

Troubleshooting
Python version: PyO3 0.20.3 builds an abi3-py39 wheel. If the extension will not import, activate the documented environment, pass its interpreter to the build and verify that you installed the resulting wheel into that same environment.
Non-Local Definitions Warning: PyO3 generates code with non-local impl warnings. Suppressed with #![allow(non_local_definitions)].
Thread Safety: The store and logger protect shared state with parking_lot locks and atomic counters. Follow the store’s lock ordering above; a cloned Record is a value, not another synchronized store.
Lazy Deletion Overhead: PriorityIndex accumulates invalidated entries. Call rebuild() periodically for long-running processes.
Event Buffer Overflow: Ring buffer overwrites oldest events. Monitor dropped_count() to detect overflow. Ensure capacity matches expected event rate.
Prost Regeneration: build.rs declares each selected schema with cargo:rerun-if-changed. Cargo reruns that build step when those inputs change. Rebuild the extension with maturin to make the regenerated types available to Python.
NaN Handling: priority_score() returns NEG_INFINITY for NaN scores, ensuring such records are pruned first.
Testing
# From the repository root
(cd kernel && cargo test)

Key tests:
test_priority_index: Heap ordering correctness
test_record_store_insert_get: Basic CRUD
test_select_for_pruning: Priority-based selection
test_ring_buffer_overflow: Buffer wrap behavior

Related guides
Architecture Overview
Python Memory Module
Protocol definitions: records, budgets, influence relations and events.
